# **S2-009 - Build the Review Q&A Interface #60**

**IssueOpen**

## Description

[@github-actions](https://github.com/apps/github-actions) ([image](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/in/15368?v=4\&size=48))

[**github-actions**](https://github.com/apps/github-actions)

**bot**

opened [3d ago](https://github.com/aum-2004/CS490_Review_Lens_AI_Fantastic_Six/issues/60#issue-6319415994)

**Outcome:**\
A user can submit a natural-language question from the active AnalysisTarget workspace and receive a ReviewLens response.

**Technical Guidance:**

At minimum, the interface should include:

1. Question input.
2. Submit action.
3. Processing/loading state.
4. Response display.
5. Meaningful error state if the AI request fails.

A full persistent chat-history system is not required.

A simple question-and-response interaction is acceptable if it supports the required analysis workflow.

The active AnalysisTarget must remain clear while the user asks questions.

**Rules:** S2-BR-008, S2-BR-014



### 4. assistant

I’ll check the requirements, UI/UX standards, and current branch, then implement S2-009 and run the relevant checks. I won’t push anything, and I’ll ask before making changes outside the story’s scope.

**Outcome:**\
A user can submit a natural-language question from the active AnalysisTarget workspace and receive a ReviewLens response.

**Technical Guidance:**

At minimum, the interface should include:

1. Question input.
2. Submit action.
3. Processing/loading state.
4. Response display.
5. Meaningful error state if the AI request fails.

A full persistent chat-history system is not required.

A simple question-and-response interaction is acceptable if it supports the required analysis workflow.

The active AnalysisTarget must remain clear while the user asks questions.

**Rules:** S2-BR-008, S2-BR-014

interface for asking natural-language questions about the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nS2-BR-009: Q&A responses must be based on reviews belonging to the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nS2-BR-010: ReviewLens must not claim review evidence that is not contained in the active dataset.\\r\\nS2-BR-011: If the available reviews do not provide sufficient evidence for an answer, ReviewLens must communicate that limitation rather than inventing information.\\r\\nS2-BR-012: The method used to provide review context to the LLM is an architectural decision for the team.\\r\\nS2-BR-013: A vector database, embeddings, or a particular RAG architecture is not required merely because the application contains AI functionality.\\r\\nS2-BR-014: The Q&A workflow must remain associated with the authenticated user's selected AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nS2-BR Scope Guard\\r\\nS2-BR-015: The system prompt must explicitly define ReviewLens as answering questions only from the active review dataset.\\r\\nS2-BR-016: General world-knowledge questions unrelated to the active reviews must be declined.\\r\\nS2-BR-017: Questions about another product, business, location, or entity not represented by the active dataset must be declined.\\r\\nS2-BR-018: Questions about another review platform must be declined when that platform's data is not contained in the active dataset.\\r\\nS2-BR-019: Scope enforcement must be driven primarily by the system prompt and supplied application context.\\r\\nS2-BR-020: Supporting application logic may reinforce the scope guard but must not replace a clear prompt-level scope definition.\\r\\nS2-BR-021: A refusal should be clear and useful to the user without pretending the requested information was analyzed.\\r\\nS2-BR Context and User Isolation\\r\\nS2-BR-022: Only review data belonging to the authenticated user may enter that user's AI context.\\r\\nS2-BR-023: Changing the active AnalysisTarget must change the review dataset used for subsequent Q&A.\\r\\nS2-BR-024: Review data from a previously selected target must not remain in the active context after the target changes.\\r\\nS2-BR-025: A target with no successfully ingested review data cannot provide a normal review-grounded answer.\\r\\nS2-BR-026: Existing Sprint 1 backend ownership rules remain authoritative for all Sprint 2 Q&A and summary operations.\\r\\nS2-BR AI Testing\\r\\nS2-BR-027: The team must maintain automated tests for the Q&A orchestration layer.\\r\\nS2-BR-028: The team must maintain a representative scope-guard evaluation set containing both accepted and rejected question types.\\r\\nS2-BR-029: CI tests must not depend on an exact natural-language response from a nondeterministic live model.\\r\\nS2-BR-030: Tests must verify behavioral properties such as accepted scope, rejected scope, correct dataset selection, and absence of cross-user context.\\r\\nS2-BR-031: Live-model testing may supplement deterministic automated tests but does not replace them.\\r\\nRule Usage in Stories and Jira\\r\\nAny Sprint 2 story may reference one or more S2-BR IDs instead of repeating the complete rule text.\\r\\nSprint 1 canonical business rules remain applicable where relevant.\\r\\nIf story behavior conflicts with a canonical business rule, the canonical business rule prevails.\\r\\nA developer implementing a story is responsible for understanding all rules referenced by that story.\\r\\nA. Sprint 2 Quality-Assurance Ratchet\\r\\nThese are primarily team-level engineering stories.\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-001 - Add Changed-Code Coverage Gate\\r\\nOutcome: The CI pipeline measures automated test coverage for changed or newly added code and rejects a pull request that fails the team's required threshold.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team may select an appropriate coverage tool and threshold for its technology stack.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe objective is not to maximize a vanity percentage. The objective is to prevent significant new behavior from entering the codebase without automated verification.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team should document:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe selected coverage mechanism.\\r\\nThe required threshold or policy.\\r\\nWhich code is excluded and why, if exclusions exist.\\r\\nHow a developer can run the coverage check locally.\\r\\nA deliberately under-tested change should be capable of causing the gate to fail.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-027 through S2-BR-031\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-002 - Add Critical Integration Test Coverage\\r\\nOutcome: The project contains automated integration tests covering important Sprint 2 boundaries between application services, persistence, ingestion data, and Q&A orchestration.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nIntegration tests should focus on boundaries where independently correct components could still fail when combined.\\r\\n\\r\\nRepresentative areas include:\\r\\n\\r\\nLoading persisted reviews for an AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nComputing an ingestion summary from persisted data.\\r\\nPassing the correct review dataset into the Q&A service.\\r\\nApplying authenticated ownership before review retrieval.\\r\\nChanging the active target and retrieving different data.\\r\\nThe exact testing technology is the team's decision.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001 through S2-BR-014, S2-BR-022 through S2-BR-030\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-003 - Create Deterministic Q&A Test Harness\\r\\nOutcome: The team can automatically test ReviewLens Q&A orchestration without depending on unpredictable live-model output.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe test harness should make it possible to verify what the application sends to and receives from the model boundary.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nMock LLM client.\\r\\nStubbed model adapter.\\r\\nRecorded model responses.\\r\\nDependency injection around the AI provider.\\r\\nEquivalent controlled testing approach.\\r\\nTests should be able to verify:\\r\\n\\r\\nCorrect system instructions are supplied.\\r\\nCorrect review context is supplied.\\r\\nWrong-target reviews are not supplied.\\r\\nCross-user reviews are not supplied.\\r\\nApplication behavior is correct for controlled model responses.\\r\\nThe test architecture should not require developers to spend money on model API calls every time CI runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-009 through S2-BR-014, S2-BR-022, S2-BR-027 through S2-BR-031\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-004 - Create Scope-Guard Evaluation Set\\r\\nOutcome: The team maintains a repeatable set of representative questions used to verify ReviewLens scope behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe evaluation set must include multiple examples from at least these categories:\\r\\n\\r\\nClearly in-scope review questions.\\r\\nRelevant questions for which the dataset lacks sufficient evidence.\\r\\nGeneral world-knowledge questions.\\r\\nQuestions about another product or entity.\\r\\nQuestions about another review platform.\\r\\nThe evaluation should determine whether the behavior is acceptable without requiring one exact answer sentence.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team may implement the evaluation as automated tests, structured fixtures, an evaluation script, or a combination.\\r\\n\\r\\nA small, thoughtful evaluation set is preferable to a large set of redundant examples.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-015 through S2-BR-021, S2-BR-027 through S2-BR-031\\r\\n\\r\\nB. Ingestion Result Summary\\r\\nS2-005 - Display Ingestion Result Status\\r\\nOutcome: The AnalysisTarget workspace clearly communicates the result state of the ingestion operation associated with the active dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user must be able to distinguish at least:\\r\\n\\r\\nSuccessful ingestion.\\r\\nFailed ingestion.\\r\\nIf the team's Sprint 1 implementation supports partial success, the UI should represent that state distinctly.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf ingestion is asynchronous, a processing state should also be represented.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe displayed result should come from persisted ingestion state rather than being inferred solely from the presence of review rows.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001, S2-BR-005 through S2-BR-007\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-006 - Display Review Count and Rating Summary\\r\\nOutcome: The user can see the number of successfully ingested reviews and basic rating information for the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, display:\\r\\n\\r\\nNumber of successfully ingested reviews.\\r\\nBasic rating information appropriate to the selected review platform.\\r\\nExamples of appropriate rating information include:\\r\\n\\r\\nAverage rating.\\r\\nRating distribution.\\r\\nCounts by rating value.\\r\\nThe team does not need to implement every possible metric.\\r\\n\\r\\nAll displayed values must be calculated from persisted review data.\\r\\n\\r\\nTests should use a known review fixture so expected values can be asserted exactly.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001 through S2-BR-004, S2-BR-007\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-007 - Report Skipped or Rejected Review Records\\r\\nOutcome: When ingestion encounters individual records that cannot be processed, the user can determine that those records were not included in the active review dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application does not need to expose raw parser diagnostics to the user.\\r\\n\\r\\nA reasonable summary may communicate:\\r\\n\\r\\nNumber successfully ingested.\\r\\nNumber skipped or rejected.\\r\\nA concise reason category when useful.\\r\\nFor example:\\r\\n\\r\\nmissing review text\\r\\ninvalid rating\\r\\nmalformed source record\\r\\nThe exact level of detail is a team design decision.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe important requirement is that unsuccessful records do not silently count as successfully analyzed data.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-005 through S2-BR-007\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-008 - Derive Summary from the Active Persisted Dataset\\r\\nOutcome: The ingestion summary accurately represents the same persisted review dataset that will be used by Q&A.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe summary should not be separately generated from stale source data, browser-only state, or LLM interpretation.\\r\\n\\r\\nTests should demonstrate that:\\r\\n\\r\\nAdding or removing a persisted test Review changes the calculated summary appropriately.\\r\\nTarget A summary uses Target A reviews.\\r\\nTarget B summary uses Target B reviews.\\r\\nUser A cannot retrieve User B's summary.\\r\\nThis story establishes a common data boundary between ingestion and analysis.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001 through S2-BR-007, S2-BR-022, S2-BR-026\\r\\n\\r\\nC. Review-Grounded Q&A\\r\\nS2-009 - Build the Review Q&A Interface\\r\\nOutcome: A user can submit a natural-language question from the active AnalysisTarget workspace and receive a ReviewLens response.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, the interface should include:\\r\\n\\r\\nQuestion input.\\r\\nSubmit action.\\r\\nProcessing/loading state.\\r\\nResponse display.\\r\\nMeaningful error state if the AI request fails.\\r\\nA full persistent chat-history system is not required.\\r\\n\\r\\nA simple question-and-response interaction is acceptable if it supports the required analysis workflow.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe active AnalysisTarget must remain clear while the user asks questions.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-008, S2-BR-014\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-010 - Build Review Dataset Context for Q&A\\r\\nOutcome: Before a question is submitted to the LLM, ReviewLens constructs AI context from reviews belonging to the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team must make an explicit architectural decision for selecting and supplying review context.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nSupplying all reviews when the dataset is small enough.\\r\\nSelecting relevant reviews before model invocation.\\r\\nRetrieval-Augmented Generation.\\r\\nEmbeddings and vector search.\\r\\nSearch or filtering strategies.\\r\\nAnother defensible approach appropriate to the team's dataset size.\\r\\nNo particular retrieval architecture is required.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe implementation must ensure:\\r\\n\\r\\nContext comes from persisted ReviewLens data.\\r\\nContext belongs to the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nContext belongs to the authenticated user.\\r\\nContext does not accidentally include a previously selected target.\\r\\nThe team should document important context-size or model-token limitations.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-009, S2-BR-012 through S2-BR-014, S2-BR-022 through S2-BR-026\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-011 - Answer Questions from Review Evidence\\r\\nOutcome: For an in-scope question supported by the active review dataset, ReviewLens produces a useful answer based on those reviews.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nRepresentative questions might include:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhat complaints appear most frequently?\\r\\nWhat do customers like about this product?\\r\\nAre there recurring complaints about customer service?\\r\\nWhat themes appear in low-rated reviews?\\r\\nWhat reasons do reviewers give f…440 tokens truncated…eview-analysis functionality\\r\\n- Review provider/API pending final team and professor approval\\r\\n\\r\\nThe exact supported versions and generated configuration are established by S1-005 and S1-006 and must be recorded in the repository lockfile and setup documentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Repository Organization\\r\\n\\r\\nThe following structure is the team's proposed baseline. S1-005 is responsible for creating and validating the actual Next.js structure. If the generated framework structure requires a change, S1-005 must update this document in the same pull request or in a linked standards pull request.\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nsrc/\\r\\n|-- app/\\r\\n|   |-- login/\\r\\n|   |-- analysis-targets/\\r\\n|   `-- api/\\r\\n|-- components/\\r\\n|   |-- ui/\\r\\n|   |-- analysis-targets/\\r\\n|   |-- ingestion/\\r\\n|   `-- shared/\\r\\n|-- services/\\r\\n|   |-- auth/\\r\\n|   |-- analysis-targets/\\r\\n|   |-- ingestion/\\r\\n|   `-- reviews/\\r\\n|-- lib/\\r\\n|   |-- supabase/\\r\\n|   |-- validation/\\r\\n|   `-- utils/\\r\\n|-- types/\\r\\n`-- proxy.ts\\r\\n\\r\\ntests/\\r\\n|-- unit/\\r\\n|-- integration/\\r\\n`-- e2e/\\r\\n\\r\\ndocs/\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nRepository rules:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Routes, layouts, pages, and Route Handlers belong under `src/app`.\\r\\n- Reusable UI belongs under `src/components`; shadcn/ui primitives belong under `src/components/ui`.\\r\\n- Business and data-access logic belongs in server-side services rather than directly in React components.\\r\\n- Route Handlers should remain thin: validate the request, authenticate the user, authorize the resource, call a service, and return a response.\\r\\n- Shared framework clients and utilities belong under `src/lib`.\\r\\n- Shared TypeScript types belong under `src/types` when they are not better located beside a single feature.\\r\\n- Unit and integration tests should mirror the application area they test. End-to-end tests belong under `tests/e2e`.\\r\\n- `public`, `package.json`, lockfiles, environment templates, and framework configuration remain at the repository root as required by Next.js.\\r\\n- With Next.js 16, request proxy logic uses `src/proxy.ts`. Authentication and authorization must not rely on Proxy alone; protected server operations must verify access independently.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Naming Conventions\\r\\n\\r\\n- React component names and component files use PascalCase, for example `TargetCard.tsx`.\\r\\n- Functions, variables, and object properties use camelCase.\\r\\n- Custom React hooks begin with `use`, for example `useAnalysisTargets.ts`.\\r\\n- Constants that are truly fixed application-wide values use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.\\r\\n- Non-component TypeScript files and feature folders use lowercase kebab-case, for example `review-parser.ts` and `analysis-targets`.\\r\\n- Test files use `.test.ts` or `.test.tsx`. Playwright files use `.spec.ts`.\\r\\n- Next.js special files keep their required framework names, including `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, and `route.ts`.\\r\\n- PostgreSQL tables and columns use snake_case.\\r\\n- Domain terminology must be consistent: use `AnalysisTarget`, `Review`, and `IngestionAttempt` in TypeScript and the corresponding snake_case names in the database.\\r\\n\\r\\nNames should describe intent. Avoid unclear abbreviations and generic names such as `data`, `thing`, or `helper` when a more specific name is available.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Formatting, Static Analysis, and Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nRequired tools:\\r\\n\\r\\n- ESLint\\r\\n- Prettier\\r\\n- TypeScript strict mode\\r\\n\\r\\nFormatting rules:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use two-space indentation.\\r\\n- Remove unused imports and variables.\\r\\n- Do not commit commented-out code or temporary debugging statements.\\r\\n- Prefer clear, typed code over unnecessary abstraction.\\r\\n- Do not suppress a TypeScript or ESLint error without explaining why in code and in the pull request.\\r\\n\\r\\nS1-006 must configure these commands in `package.json`:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `npm run lint`\\r\\n- `npm run format:check`\\r\\n- `npm run test`\\r\\n- `npm run build`\\r\\n\\r\\nAll applicable commands must pass before a code pull request is merged. Until S1-006 establishes the scripts, contributors must not claim that an unconfigured check has passed.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Error-Handling Conventions\\r\\n\\r\\n- Validate external input at an authoritative server boundary even when the browser also validates it.\\r\\n- Handle expected errors explicitly and translate them into safe, understandable responses.\\r\\n- Do not expose stack traces, SQL details, internal file paths, secrets, credentials, or provider responses containing sensitive information.\\r\\n- Unexpected errors must be logged safely on the server and returned to the user as a generic error.\\r\\n- Existing valid review data must not be replaced by fabricated or placeholder data when ingestion fails.\\r\\n\\r\\nStandard HTTP status usage:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `200` - successful request\\r\\n- `201` - resource created\\r\\n- `400` - invalid request or validation failure\\r\\n- `401` - authentication required or invalid session\\r\\n- `403` - authenticated user is not permitted to perform the operation\\r\\n- `404` - requested resource is unavailable or cannot be disclosed\\r\\n- `409` - conflict, such as an operation that violates a uniqueness rule\\r\\n- `500` - unexpected server failure\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team must apply a consistent `403`/`404` policy to user-owned resources so responses do not reveal another user's private resource. The selected policy must be tested.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. API and Service Response Conventions\\r\\n\\r\\nSuccessful Route Handler response:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"success\\\": true,\\r\\n  \\\"data\\\": {}\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nError response:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"success\\\": false,\\r\\n  \\\"error\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"code\\\": \\\"INVALID_SOURCE_URL\\\",\\r\\n    \\\"message\\\": \\\"The submitted source URL is invalid.\\\"\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nRules:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Error `code` values are stable machine-readable identifiers; `message` values are safe user-readable explanations.\\r\\n- Validation responses may include safe field-level details when useful.\\r\\n- Route Handlers must use the shared response convention instead of inventing a new shape per endpoint.\\r\\n- Service functions return typed results or throw documented application errors; they do not return ad hoc response objects.\\r\\n- Protected endpoints derive identity from the verified Supabase session, never from a client-supplied owner ID.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 8. Authentication, Authorization, and Ownership\\r\\n\\r\\n- Every AnalysisTarget belongs to exactly one authenticated user.\\r\\n- Review and IngestionAttempt access is authorized through the owning AnalysisTarget.\\r\\n- Protected Route Handlers must verify the session, derive authenticated identity, verify resource ownership, and only then perform the operation.\\r\\n- The frontend may improve navigation by hiding unavailable actions, but frontend filtering is never an authorization control.\\r\\n- Client-supplied `userId`, `ownerId`, or equivalent values are not trusted for ownership decisions.\\r\\n- Supabase RLS provides defense in depth but does not replace authorization inside protected server operations.\\r\\n- Cross-user tests must use at least two identities and prove that User B cannot read, modify, delete, or ingest into User A's resources.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 9. Logging Expectations\\r\\n\\r\\nLog server-side events that help diagnose or audit the system, including:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Authentication and authorization failures\\r\\n- Ingestion start, success, partial success, and failure\\r\\n- External-provider failures\\r\\n- Database failures\\r\\n- Unexpected application failures\\r\\n\\r\\nLogs should include safe context such as operation name, error category, and a request or correlation identifier when available.\\r\\n\\r\\nNever log:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Passwords\\r\\n- Session cookies, authentication tokens, or authorization headers\\r\\n- API keys, database credentials, or complete environment values\\r\\n- Supabase service-role keys\\r\\n- Unredacted personal information\\r\\n- Full customer-review text in routine production logs\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the shared project logger once it is established. Do not leave temporary `console.log` debugging statements in merged code.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 10. Adding and Updating Dependencies\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team uses npm and commits `package-lock.json`. Do not use Yarn or pnpm in this repository.\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore adding a dependency:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Confirm that it solves a specific project need.\\r\\n2. Confirm that an existing dependency or platform capability does not already solve the problem.\\r\\n3. Verify that the package is actively maintained and compatible with the project's Node.js and Next.js versions.\\r\\n4. Review its license and known security concerns.\\r\\n5. Place it in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` correctly.\\r\\n6. Explain the addition in the pull request.\\r\\n\\r\\nInstall packages through npm rather than manually editing dependency versions. Unrelated dependency upgrades must not be included in a feature pull request.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 11. Testing Standards\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery code change that adds or modifies behavior must include appropriate automated tests. Documentation-only changes should state that automated tests are not applicable and identify the review performed instead.\\r\\n\\r\\nDepending on the behavior, tests should cover:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Successful behavior\\r\\n- Expected failure behavior\\r\\n- Validation boundaries\\r\\n- Authenticated and unauthenticated requests\\r\\n- Authorized and unauthorized users\\r\\n- Persistence and ownership where applicable\\r\\n- Loading and error states for interactive UI\\r\\n\\r\\nExternal review-provider APIs and OpenAI calls must be mocked or replaced with deterministic fixtures in CI. Automated tests must not depend entirely on a live external website or paid provider.\\r\\n\\r\\nSecurity-sensitive features require explicit User A/User B isolation tests. A test must demonstrate denial at the backend or database boundary, not merely that the other user's record is hidden in the UI.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 12. AI-Assisted Development\\r\\n\\r\\nAI-generated code is treated as team-authored code and must meet the same standards and Definition of Done.\\r\\n\\r\\nDevelopers must:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Provide the relevant story, architecture, standards, and existing code as prompt context.\\r\\n- Review and understand generated changes before accepting them.\\r\\n- Verify generated APIs, packages, and configuration against authoritative documentation.\\r\\n- Test generated behavior, including failure and security cases.\\r\\n- Retain the required AI-session transcript according to the convention established by S1-004.\\r\\n- Request additional human review for authentication, authorization, RLS, secret handling, ingestion, and AI-data-boundary changes.\\r\\n\\r\\nAI output is a proposal, not proof that a change is correct.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 13. Pull Request Requirements\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery pull request must:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Link the relevant GitHub issue.\\r\\n- Describe what changed and why.\\r\\n- Stay within the assigned story's scope.\\r\\n- Identify tests or review evidence.\\r\\n- Pass all applicable build, formatting, lint, and automated-test checks.\\r\\n- Contain no real secrets or unrelated generated files.\\r\\n- Receive approval from at least one teammate before merge.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe author must respond to review feedback. A pull request is not Done until it is approved, required checks pass, it is merged into `main`, and the associated board item is updated.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 14. Environment and Secret Requirements\\r\\n\\r\\n- Real secrets must never be committed.\\r\\n- Local secrets belong in `.env.local`, which must be ignored by Git.\\r\\n- `.env.example` documents required variable names using empty or clearly fake placeholder values.\\r\\n- Variables beginning with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are exposed to the browser and must never contain private credentials.\\r\\n- Supabase service-role keys, database credentials, OpenAI keys, and private provider credentials are server-only.\\r\\n- Environment-specific values must not be hard-coded into source files.\\r\\n- Missing required configuration must produce a clear startup or runtime error without exposing the secret value.\\r\\n- If a secret is accidentally committed, stop using it, notify the team, rotate or revoke it immediately, and follow the team's incident procedure. Deleting it from the latest file alone is not sufficient.\\r\\n\\r\\nS1-008 owns the final `.env.example`, ignore rules, environment-validation approach, and setup instructions. When S1-008 changes these conventions, this document must remain consistent with that implementation.\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\index.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\04-community\\\\index.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\04-community\\\\02-rspack.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\04-community\\\\01-contribution-guide.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\01-app\\\\index.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\01-app\\\\04-glossary.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\03-architecture\\\\supported-browsers.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\03-architecture\\\\nextjs-compiler.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\03-architecture\\\\index.md\\r\\nnode_modules/next/dist/docs\\\\03-architecture\\\\fast-refresh.md\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n    Directory: [absolute filesystem path removed]"}"

Stack columns, never hide required actions and let wide content scroll inside its own container instead of scrolling the whole page.\\r\\n\\r\\n**3\\\\. Form conventions**  \\r\\nApplies to: AuthForm, TargetForm, and any other future form.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Library:** Form built with React Hook Form and shared Zod schemas(or other equivalent), using shadcn/ui Form, Input, Label, and Button. Also set aria-required=\\\"true\\\".\\r\\n4. **Help text:** Muted text-sm text beneath the input linked with aria-describedby.\\r\\n5. **Field order and Naming for TargetForm:**\\r\\n   1. **Target name \\\\*:** text input, e.g \\\"NJIT, Newark\\\".\\r\\n   2. **Review platform:** Shown as a read-only field/badge fixed to Google Maps.\\r\\n   3. **Google Maps URL \\\\*:** URL input.\\r\\n6. **Actions:** Primary submit button on the right \\\"Create target\\\", secondary \\\"Cancel\\\" button to its left. Pressing Enter in a field submits the form.\\r\\n7. **Input behavior:** Trim leading/trailing whitespace before validating. Do not clear the user's input on a failed submit. Autofocus the first invalid field after a failed submit.\\r\\n8. **Submit protection:**While submitting, the submit button is disabled and shows a spinner so the form cannot be double-submitted.\\r\\n9. **Success:** After a successful creation, navigate to the new target's workspace, which shows a success alert (\\\"Target created. You can now start ingestion.\\\") at the top of the page. The alert stays in place until the user leaves the page.\\r\\n10. **AuthForm:** Sign In and Register share one AuthForm component with a clearly labeled toggle. Fields: Email \\\\*, Password\\\\*. Validation and error presentation**  \\r\\nValidation runs in two places: client for fast feedback and server as authoritative check (per S1-BR-015). The client will never replace the server check and UI must display server validation errors the same way as client ones.\\r\\n\\r\\n4.1 Target input validation  \\r\\nA target is rejected and nothing is persisted unless all of these rules are met. These rules are implemented once in a shared schema and re-run on the server.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Field       | Rule                                                                                                        | Message shown to the user                                                                                                           |\\r\\n| :---------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| Target name | Required, cannot be whitespace, cannot be empty                                                             | \\\"Enter a name for this target.\\\"                                                                                                     |\\r\\n| Target name | Cannot contain unsafe control characters.                                                                   | \\\"Target names can't contain control characters.\\\"                                                                                    |\\r\\n| Target name | Max Length 120                                                                                              | \\\"Target names can be up to 120 characters.\\\"                                                                                         |\\r\\n| Source URL  | Required, cannot be whitespace, cannot be empty.                                                            | \\\"Enter the Google Maps link for this target.\\\"                                                                                       |\\r\\n| Source URL  | Must be a well-formed http(s) URL                                                                           | \\\"That doesn't look like a valid web address. Paste the full link, starting with https\\\\://.\\\"                                         |\\r\\n| Source URL  | Cannot exceed 2,048 characters, including after canonical URL encoding.                                     | \\\"Google Maps links can be up to 2,048 characters.\\\"                                                                                  |\\r\\n| Source URL  | Must correspond to Google Maps. Accepted Google Maps hostnames are defined in the shared validation schema. | \\\"This link isn't a Google Maps link. Open the full Google Maps URL in your browser and copy it from the address bar.\\\" |\\r\\n\\r\\n4.2 Valid input succeeds and each message above is covered by an automated test for both accepted and rejected input.\\r\\n\\r\\nError presentation:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Inline field error:** red text-sm message directly beneath the offending field, linked via aria-describedby, with the input marked aria-invalid=\\\"true\\\" and a red border. Each message includes an error icon so color is not the only signal the user sees.\\r\\n2. **Form-level summary:** If the form has two or more errors, show an alert at the top of the form (\\\"Please fix the highlighted fields.\\\") with role=\\\"alert\\\".\\r\\n3. **Timing:** Validate on submit first, after the first failed submit, re-validate each field on blur and on change. Do not show errors on untouched fields.\\r\\n4. **Server-side validation errors** arrive as structured field errors and are mapped to the same inline error slots. Never show a raw JSON payload.\\r\\n\\r\\n4.3 Error categories (as per S1-BR-025) and presentation\\r\\n\\r\\n| Category                       | Where shown                                        | Example message                                                                                                                                              |\\r\\n| :----------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| Validation failure             | Inline under fields                                | See 4.1                                                                                                                                                      |\\r\\n| Authentication failure         | Alert on /login, or redirect to /login with notice | Bad credentials: \\\"We couldn't sign you in. Check your email and password and try again.\\\" Session expiration: \\\"Your session has ended. Please sign in again.\\\" |\\r\\n| Authorization denial           | Full-page error state in the content area          | \\\"This target isn't available to your account. Go back to My Targets.\\\" No target data is rendered, and the page does not confirm whether the target exists.   |\\r\\n| Ingestion failure              | Inline ErrorAlert in the IngestionPanel            | See 4.4                                                                                                                                                      |\\r\\n| Unexpected application failure | ErrorAlert or full-page error boundary             | \\\"Something went wrong on our side. Please try again in a moment.\\\"                                                                                            |\\r\\n\\r\\n4.4 Ingestion errors (S1-BR-025)\\r\\n\\r\\n| Situation                         | Message shown to the user                                                                                   | Suggested next step                                          |\\r\\n| :-------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| Source URL invalid or unusable    | \\\"We couldn't find reviews at this link. Check that the link opens a Google Maps page.\\\"                      | Check the link, or create a new target with a different link |\\r\\n| Source returned no usable reviews | \\\"No usable reviews were found for this source, so nothing was saved.\\\"                                       | Create a new target with a different link                    |\\r\\n| Provider times out                | \\\"The review service took too long to respond. Please try again.\\\"                                            | Retry                                                        |\\r\\n| Provider quota exhausted          | \\\"Review collection is temporarily unavailable because our usage limit was reached. Please try again later.\\\" | Try again later                                              |\\r\\n| Provider unreachable              | \\\"We couldn't reach the review service. Please try again later.\\\"                                             | Retry                                                        |\\r\\n\\r\\n4.5 Error text rules:  \\r\\nPlain language, three sentences max, and a next step if applicable. Never display stack traces, database messages, HTTP client exceptions, provider SDK or API error text, internal IDs, or secrets. Technical detail only goes to server logs. A failed ingestion never shows reviews that were not actually collected and previously saved reviews remain visible and unchanged.  \\r\\nErrors that appear after an action use role=\\\"alert\\\" so screen readers announce them. Errors stay in place until the user retries the action or leaves the page; do not auto dismiss errors.\\r\\n\\r\\n**5\\\\. Loading and processing states**\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Page/data loading:** Use shadcn/ui Skeleton placeholders that match the final layout (title bar plus card or grid shapes). Do not use a bare full-page spinner for page loads.\\r\\n2. **Button/action in progress:** The button is disabled, its label changes to the progressive form (\\\"Creatingâ€¦\\\", \\\"Starting ingestion...\\\"), and a small spinner appears before the label. Keep the button width stable.\\r\\n3. **Spinner component:** One shared spinner component. No one builds a second loading indicator\\r\\n4. **Never leave the user wondering:** Any action that takes more than 500 ms shows a visible processing state and the UI never shows stale success while a new request is running.\\r\\n5. **Ingestion status model:** IngestionStatus is the single component that renders Ingestion state, using the same badge everywhere (target card, workspace header, ingestion panel):\\r\\n\\r\\n| State                          | Badge label        | Color        | Panel behavior                                                                                                                                  |\\r\\n| :----------------------------- | :----------------- | :----------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| No ingestion has occurred      | Not ingested       | Neutral gray | Shows \\\"Start ingestion\\\" as the primary action and a one-line explanation.                                                                       |\\r\\n| Processing                     | Ingesting          | Blue         | \\\"Start ingestion\\\" is disabled; text states which target and source are being processed; status refreshes automatically until it ends.           |\\r\\n| Succeeded                      | Ingested           | Green        | Shows the number of reviews saved; ReviewList shows the persisted reviews                                                                       |\\r\\n| Succeeded with skipped records | Partially ingested | Amber        | Shows saved and skipped counts, explains that only saved reviews enter the dataset, and retains the existing completed-run action restrictions. |\\r\\n| Failed                         | Failed             | Red          | Shows the ErrorAlert from 4.4 and a \\\"Try again\\\" button, prior data must remain                                                                  |\\r\\n\\r\\nPartial completion is derived from persisted `succeeded` status with a positive\\r\\n`skipped_count`; it does not introduce a new database state. The badge requires\\r\\n`skippedCount` explicitly. Missing, negative, non-integer, or non-finite counts\\r\\ndisplay \\\"Status unavailable\\\" rather than suggesting complete success. Unavailable\\r\\nstate also displays \\\"Status unavailable\\\" and never implies \\\"Not ingested\\\".\\r\\n\\r\\n6. **Processing context:** While ingesting, the panel states the active target and source (\\\"Collecting reviews for {target name} from Google Mapsâ€¦\\\") so the user knows what is happening and where results will go.\\r\\n7. **Navigating away:** Leaving the workspace during ingestion does not cancel it. Returning shows the current state fetched from the server.\\r\\n8. **Reduced motion:** Respect prefers-reduced-motion by replacing spinner/skeleton animation with static indicators\\r\\n\\r\\n**6\\\\. Button and action conventions**\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Component:** Use shadcn/ui Button only. Variants: default(primary), outline(Secondary), ghost (tertiary/inline), destructive\\r\\n2. **One primary action per view region:**A page header or card holds at most one default button. Avoid \\\"Submit\\\", \\\"OK\\\", and \\\"Click here\\\".\\r\\n4. **Placement:** In forms and dialogs, primary action on the right with Cancel to its left. In page headers, the primary page action sits at the right.\\r\\n5. **Sizing:** Default height 40px, icon only buttons must have an aria-label.\\r\\n6. **States:** Every button has a distinct hover, focus-visible ring (2px), disabled (reduced opacity, cursor-not-allowed), and loading states.\\r\\n7. **Disabled actions:** when an action is unavailable, disable it and explain why in nearby text. Do not silently remove actions.\\r\\n8. **Links vs buttons:** Navigation uses links, actions that change data use buttons. Never use a clickable div.\\r\\n9. **Destructive actions:** Deleting a target uses destructive styling plus a confirmation dialog naming the target. Do not add it early without approval.\\r\\n10. **Where actions live:** \\\"New Target\\\" in the top bar only; \\\"Create target\\\" and \\\"Cancel\\\" in TargetForm; \\\"Start ingestion\\\" and \\\"Try again\\\" in IngestionPanel only; \\\"Sign out\\\" in the account menu only.\\r\\n\\r\\n**7\\\\. Spacing and typography**  \\r\\n7.1 Typography\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Font:** Inter, loaded once through next/font, with the system sans-serif stack as fallback. A monospace stack is allowed only for URLs shown as code, if needed.\\r\\n2. **Type scale (Tailwind)**\\r\\n\\r\\n| Use             | Class     | Weight                   |\\r\\n| :-------------- | :-------- | :----------------------- |\\r\\n| Page title h1   | text-3xl  | font-semibold            |\\r\\n| Card title h2   | text-xl   | font-semibold            |\\r\\n| Sub-heading h3  | text-lg   | font-medium              |\\r\\n| Body            | text-base | font-normal              |\\r\\n| Secondary text  | text-sm   | font-normal, muted color |\\r\\n| Badges, caption | text-xs   | font-medium              |\\r\\n\\r\\n**Line height:** Use Tailwind defaults paired with each size. Body text maximum line width about 70 characters. Exactly one h1 per page, with headings in order and never skipped for styling reasons.\\r\\n\\r\\n7.2 Color tokens  \\r\\nUse only the semantic tokens defined in the Tailwind theme (the shadcn/ui defaults plus success, info, and warning).\\r\\n\\r\\n| Token                       | Purpose                                                                                        |\\r\\n| :-------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| Primary                     | Primary buttons, links, focus accents                                                          |\\r\\n| foreground/muted-foreground | Body and secondary text                                                                        |\\r\\n| background/card/border      | Surfaces and dividers                                                                          |\\r\\n| destructive                 | Errors, failed state                                                                           |\\r\\n| success                     | Succeeded state (a custom token defined in the theme, green)                                   |\\r\\n| info                        | Processing state (blue)                                                                        |\\r\\n| warning                     | Partial ingestion (amber), distinct from processing blue; dark-mode value defined in the theme |\\r\\n\\r\\nText and interactive elements must meet WCAG AA contrast for user accessibility.  \\r\\n7.3 Spacing\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **4px base unit** using the Tailwind spacing scale only. Error and Failure Experience\\r\\nReviewLens depends on multiple application and external-service boundaries, so failure states are part of the normal user experience.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should distinguish among:\\r\\n\\r\\nInvalid AnalysisTarget input.\\r\\nAuthentication or session failure.\\r\\nAuthorization denial.\\r\\nReview-source or ingestion failure.\\r\\nPartial or incomplete ingestion.\\r\\nNo review data available.\\r\\nLLM-provider failure.\\r\\nUnexpected application failure.\\r\\nErrors should be expressed in user terms rather than implementation terms.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not present normal users with:\\r\\n\\r\\nRaw stack traces.\\r\\nDatabase exceptions.\\r\\nProvider SDK errors.\\r\\nInternal authentication-provider messages.\\r\\nSecret values.\\r\\nUnnecessary technical diagnostics.\\r\\nWhere practical, failure messages should also communicate what the user can do next.\\r\\n\\r\\nExamples include:\\r\\n\\r\\nCorrect invalid input.\\r\\nRetry ingestion later.\\r\\nComplete ingestion before asking questions.\\r\\nAsk a question about the active reviews.\\r\\nTry the AI operation again when the provider is available.\\r\\n10. Visual Language\\r\\nThe visual direction should be modern, student-friendly, and professional.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application should feel current without becoming noisy or overly decorative.\\r\\n\\r\\nTeams may choose their own design style, but they should establish a visual system early and apply it consistently.\\r\\n\\r\\nTypography, spacing, color, and component styling should be deliberate.\\r\\n\\r\\nRepeated UI elements should look and behave as though they belong to the same product family.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis includes:\\r\\n\\r\\nButtons.\\r\\nForms.\\r\\nCards and panels.\\r\\nNavigation.\\r\\nStatus indicators.\\r\\nLoading states.\\r\\nValidation.\\r\\nError states.\\r\\nIngestion states.\\r\\nQ&A responses.\\r\\nReviewLens should look like a modern analysis product rather than a collection of developer tools or an unstyled generic chatbot.\\r\\n\\r\\n11. Responsive Behavior\\r\\nReviewLens is desktop-first.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe primary workflows are expected to be used primarily on desktop and laptop computers, and teams should optimize those experiences first.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt the same time, the application should remain usable and understandable on tablets and mobile devices.\\r\\n\\r\\nResponsive support should be intentional rather than an afterthought.\\r\\n\\r\\nCore workflows should not become unusable merely because the screen is smaller.\\r\\n\\r\\nA Progressive Web App implementation is optional.\\r\\n\\r\\nIt may be included if a team chooses to invest in it, but it is not required.\\r\\n\\r\\n12. Production Experience Expectations\\r\\nBy the final sprint, ReviewLens should feel like a production application rather than a development environment exposed to the internet.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe public application should:\\r\\n\\r\\nLoad into a coherent product experience.\\r\\nPreserve the navigation and interaction patterns established earlier.\\r\\nUse deliberate loading states.\\r\\nHandle missing or unavailable external services gracefully.\\r\\nAvoid exposing developer-only debug information.\\r\\nAvoid exposing raw errors or configuration details.\\r\\nPreserve user context and persisted data across sessions.\\r\\nContinue to make the active AnalysisTarget clear.\\r\\nProduction deployment should not introduce an entirely different user experience from the development application.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application should feel like the same product throughout the semester.\\r\\n\\r\\n13. UX Quality Standard\\r\\nThe primary UX quality goals are:\\r\\n\\r\\nConsistency\\r\\nRepeated actions, controls, states, and interaction patterns should behave the same way throughout the application.\\r\\n\\r\\nClarity\\r\\nUsers should understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget is active.\\r\\nWhat review data is available.\\r\\nWhat action they can take.\\r\\nWhat just happened.\\r\\nWhether ReviewLens answered, lacked evidence, refused the question, or encountered a technical failure.\\r\\nFlow\\r\\nUsers should be able to move naturally through:\\r\\n\\r\\nTarget selection â†’ Ingestion â†’ Dataset understanding â†’ Review Q&A\\r\\n\\r\\nwithout becoming lost or losing context.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a team makes creative layout and interaction choices while preserving consistency, clarity, and flow, that is exactly the kind of result this project should produce.\\r\\n\\r\\n  main\\n* Upon reading this document, any two developers can build pages that are recognizably consistent with each other.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules applied to this document:\\r\\n\\r\\n**S1-BR-003**: Authentication is required for all protected ReviewLens application functionality.  \\r\\n**S1-BR-015**: Required target information must be validated before the target is accepted.\\r\\n\\r\\n**S1-BR-025**: Invalid or unusable ingestion input must produce a meaningful application error.\\r\\n\\r\\nTable of Contents\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Application navigation**  \\r\\nPattern: One top navigation bar inside a single AppShell that wraps every protected page (S1-BR-003). No sidebars or a different style on any screen.  \\r\\nRules:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **AppShell:** AppShell wraps every authenticated page. Contains the top bar and the page content area.\\r\\n2. **Top bar contents from left to right:** ReviewLens wordmark that links to /analysis-targets, navigation link \\\"My Targets\\\", a primary button \\\"New Target\\\", and, at the far right of the top bar, an account menu showing the signed in email plus a \\\"Sign out\\\" item.\\r\\n3. **Active context:** When the user is inside a target(/analysis-targets/{targetId})(not including /analysis-targets/new), the page header always shows the target name and platform. The top bar never changes between pages.\\r\\n4. **Breadcrumbs:** The Target Workspace and Create Target shows a breadcrumb above the page title: (My Targets > {Target name}) or (My Targets > New Target).\\\"My Targets\\\" is a link.\\r\\n5. **Route map:**\\r\\n\\r\\n| Screen            | Route                        | Access                                                             |\\r\\n| :---------------- | :--------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| Sign In/ Register | /login                       | Public                                                             |\\r\\n| Home              | /                            | Public. Redirects to /analysis-targets if signed in, /login if not |\\r\\n| My Targets        | /analysis-targets            | Protected                                                          |\\r\\n| Create Target     | /analysis-targets/new        | Protected                                                          |\\r\\n| Target Workspace  | /analysis-targets/{targetId} | Protected                                                          |\\r\\n| Page not found    | Any other route              | Public                                                             |\\r\\n\\r\\n6. **Protected-route behavior (S1-BR-003**): An unauthenticated visit to any protected route listed in the route map redirects to /login and after a successful sign-in, returns the user to the originally requested route. The sign-in page shows the neutral notice \\\"Please sign in to continue.\\\". Until the session is resolved, the page shows a loading skeleton and renders no protected data. Route guards such as this are UX conveniences only and the backend independently rejects unauthenticated requests. A 401 or expired session redirects to /login.\\r\\n7. **Sign out:** The \\\"sign out\\\" menu item on the top bar ends the session and redirects the user to /login. After sign-out, browser Back shows /login and no protected data.\\r\\n8. **Keyboard actions:** All navigation items are reachable by TAB in visual order, visually represented by a visible focus ring. ENTER or SPACE opens the account menu and closes with escape. \\\"Skip to main content\\\" link is the first focusable element in AppShell.\\r\\n\\r\\n**2\\\\. Page layout**  \\r\\nAll pages must follow these rules if the page uses components mentioned in this list.  \\r\\n**/login does not use AppShell and gets a minimal centered layout and form with no top bar.**\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Container:** Page content sits in a centered container with max-w-6xl(1152px). Form only pages use max-w-xl.\\r\\n2. **Vertical structure of every protected page:** top bar, breadcrumb(when it's applicable), page header, and page made of cards.\\r\\n3. **Page header:** An h1 page title and the primary page action aligned right on desktop.\\r\\n4. **Target workspace header:** Displays in the order of target name, platform badge, source, and current ingestion status badge.\\r\\n5. **Workspace body:** Two stacked cards: Ingestion and reviews(ReviewList of persistent reviews). Ingestion is the IngestionPanel with \\\"Start ingestion\\\" action, IngestionStatus, and last run details.\\r\\n6. **Cards:** shadcn/ui Card with rounded-lg border bg-card shadow-sm, internal padding p-6, card title should be an h2. Stack columns, never hide required actions and let wide content scroll inside its own container instead of scrolling the whole page.\\r\\n\\r\\n**3\\\\. Paste the full link, starting with https\\\\://.\\\"                                         |\\r\\n| Source URL  | Cannot exceed 2,048 characters, including after canonical URL encoding.                                     | \\\"Google Maps links can be up to 2,048 characters.\\\"                                                                                  |\\r\\n| Source URL  | Must correspond to Google Maps. Open the full Google Maps URL in your browser and copy it from the address bar.\\\" |\\r\\n\\r\\n4.2 Valid input succeeds and each message above is covered by an automated test for both accepted and rejected input.\\r\\n\\r\\nError presentation:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Inline field error:** red text-sm message directly beneath the offending field, linked via aria-describedby, with the input marked aria-invalid=\\\"true\\\" and a red border. Keep the button width stable.\\r\\n3. **Spinner component:** One shared spinner component. No one builds a second loading indicator\\r\\n4. **Never leave the user wondering:** Any action that takes more than 500 ms shows a visible processing state and the UI never shows stale success while a new request is running.\\r\\n5. **Ingestion status model:** IngestionStatus is the single component that renders Ingestion state, using the same badge everywhere (target card, workspace header, ingestion panel):\\r\\n\\r\\n| State                          | Badge label        | Color        | Panel behavior                                                                                                                                  |\\r\\n| :----------------------------- | :----------------- | :----------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| No ingestion has occurred      | Not ingested       | Neutral gray | Shows \\\"Start ingestion\\\" as the primary action and a one-line explanation.                                                                       |\\r\\n| Processing                     | Ingesting          | Blue         | \\\"Start ingestion\\\" is disabled; text states which target and source are being processed; status refreshes automatically until it ends.           |\\r\\n| Succeeded                      | Ingested           | Green        | Shows the number of reviews saved; it does not introduce a new database state. verify behavioral properties such as accepted scope, rejected scope, correct dataset selection, and absence of cross-user context.\\r\\nS2-BR-031: Live-model testing may supplement deterministic
