canonical business rules remain applicable where relevant.\\r\\nIf story behavior conflicts with a canonical business rule, the canonical business rule prevails.\\r\\nA developer implementing a story is responsible for understanding all rules referenced by that story.\\r\\nA. Sprint 2 Quality-Assurance Ratchet\\r\\nThese are primarily team-level engineering stories.\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-001 - Add Changed-Code Coverage Gate\\r\\nOutcome: The CI pipeline measures automated test coverage for changed or newly added code and rejects a pull request that fails the team's required threshold.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team may select an appropriate coverage tool and threshold for its technology stack.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe objective is not to maximize a vanity percentage. The objective is to prevent significant new behavior from entering the codebase without automated verification.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team should document:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe selected coverage mechanism.\\r\\nThe required threshold or policy.\\r\\nWhich code is excluded and why, if exclusions exist.\\r\\nHow a developer can run the coverage check locally.\\r\\nA deliberately under-tested change should be capable of causing the gate to fail.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-027 through S2-BR-031\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-002 - Add Critical Integration Test Coverage\\r\\nOutcome: The project contains automated integration tests covering important Sprint 2 boundaries between application services, persistence, ingestion data, and Q&A orchestration.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nIntegration tests should focus on boundaries where independently correct components could still fail when combined.\\r\\n\\r\\nRepresentative areas include:\\r\\n\\r\\nLoading persisted reviews for an AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nComputing an ingestion summary from persisted data.\\r\\nPassing the correct review dataset into the Q&A service.\\r\\nApplying authenticated ownership before review retrieval.\\r\\nChanging the active target and retrieving different data.\\r\\nThe exact testing technology is the team's decision.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001 through S2-BR-014, S2-BR-022 through S2-BR-030\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-003 - Create Deterministic Q&A Test Harness\\r\\nOutcome: The team can automatically test ReviewLens Q&A orchestration without depending on unpredictable live-model output.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe test harness should make it possible to verify what the application sends to and receives from the model boundary.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nMock LLM client.\\r\\nStubbed model adapter.\\r\\nRecorded model responses.\\r\\nDependency injection around the AI provider.\\r\\nEquivalent controlled testing approach.\\r\\nTests should be able to verify:\\r\\n\\r\\nCorrect system instructions are supplied.\\r\\nCorrect review context is supplied.\\r\\nWrong-target reviews are not supplied.\\r\\nCross-user reviews are not supplied.\\r\\nApplication behavior is correct for controlled model responses.\\r\\nThe test architecture should not require developers to spend money on model API calls every time CI runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-009 through S2-BR-014, S2-BR-022, S2-BR-027 through S2-BR-031\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-004 - Create Scope-Guard Evaluation Set\\r\\nOutcome: The team maintains a repeatable set of representative questions used to verify ReviewLens scope behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe evaluation set must include multiple examples from at least these categories:\\r\\n\\r\\nClearly in-scope review questions.\\r\\nRelevant questions for which the dataset lacks sufficient evidence.\\r\\nGeneral world-knowledge questions.\\r\\nQuestions about another product or entity.\\r\\nQuestions about another review platform.\\r\\nThe evaluation should determine whether the behavior is acceptable without requiring one exact answer sentence.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team may implement the evaluation as automated tests, structured fixtures, an evaluation script, or a combination.\\r\\n\\r\\nA small, thoughtful evaluation set is preferable to a large set of redundant examples.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-015 through S2-BR-021, S2-BR-027 through S2-BR-031\\r\\n\\r\\nB. Ingestion Result Summary\\r\\nS2-005 - Display Ingestion Result Status\\r\\nOutcome: The AnalysisTarget workspace clearly communicates the result state of the ingestion operation associated with the active dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user must be able to distinguish at least:\\r\\n\\r\\nSuccessful ingestion.\\r\\nFailed ingestion.\\r\\nIf the team's Sprint 1 implementation supports partial success, the UI should represent that state distinctly.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf ingestion is asynchronous, a processing state should also be represented.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe displayed result should come from persisted ingestion state rather than being inferred solely from the presence of review rows.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001, S2-BR-005 through S2-BR-007\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-006 - Display Review Count and Rating Summary\\r\\nOutcome: The user can see the number of successfully ingested reviews and basic rating information for the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, display:\\r\\n\\r\\nNumber of successfully ingested reviews.\\r\\nBasic rating information appropriate to the selected review platform.\\r\\nExamples of appropriate rating information include:\\r\\n\\r\\nAverage rating.\\r\\nRating distribution.\\r\\nCounts by rating value.\\r\\nThe team does not need to implement every possible metric.\\r\\n\\r\\nAll displayed values must be calculated from persisted review data.\\r\\n\\r\\nTests should use a known review fixture so expected values can be asserted exactly.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001 through S2-BR-004, S2-BR-007\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-007 - Report Skipped or Rejected Review Records\\r\\nOutcome: When ingestion encounters individual records that cannot be processed, the user can determine that those records were not included in the active review dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application does not need to expose raw parser diagnostics to the user.\\r\\n\\r\\nA reasonable summary may communicate:\\r\\n\\r\\nNumber successfully ingested.\\r\\nNumber skipped or rejected.\\r\\nA concise reason category when useful.\\r\\nFor example:\\r\\n\\r\\nmissing review text\\r\\ninvalid rating\\r\\nmalformed source record\\r\\nThe exact level of detail is a team design decision.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe important requirement is that unsuccessful records do not silently count as successfully analyzed data.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-005 through S2-BR-007\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-008 - Derive Summary from the Active Persisted Dataset\\r\\nOutcome: The ingestion summary accurately represents the same persisted review dataset that will be used by Q&A.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe summary should not be separately generated from stale source data, browser-only state, or LLM interpretation.\\r\\n\\r\\nTests should demonstrate that:\\r\\n\\r\\nAdding or removing a persisted test Review changes the calculated summary appropriately.\\r\\nTarget A summary uses Target A reviews.\\r\\nTarget B summary uses Target B reviews.\\r\\nUser A cannot retrieve User B's summary.\\r\\nThis story establishes a common data boundary between ingestion and analysis.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-001 through S2-BR-007, S2-BR-022, S2-BR-026\\r\\n\\r\\nC. Review-Grounded Q&A\\r\\nS2-009 - Build the Review Q&A Interface\\r\\nOutcome: A user can submit a natural-language question from the active AnalysisTarget workspace and receive a ReviewLens response.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, the interface should include:\\r\\n\\r\\nQuestion input.\\r\\nSubmit action.\\r\\nProcessing/loading state.\\r\\nResponse display.\\r\\nMeaningful error state if the AI request fails.\\r\\nA full persistent chat-history system is not required.\\r\\n\\r\\nA simple question-and-response interaction is acceptable if it supports the required analysis workflow.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe active AnalysisTarget must remain clear while the user asks questions.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-008, S2-BR-014\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-010 - Build Review Dataset Context for Q&A\\r\\nOutcome: Before a question is submitted to the LLM, ReviewLens constructs AI context from reviews belonging to the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team must make an explicit architectural decision for selecting and supplying review context.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nSupplying all reviews when the dataset is small enough.\\r\\nSelecting relevant reviews before model invocation.\\r\\nRetrieval-Augmented Generation.\\r\\nEmbeddings and vector search.\\r\\nSearch or filtering strategies.\\r\\nAnother defensible approach appropriate to the team's dataset size.\\r\\nNo particular retrieval architecture is required.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe implementation must ensure:\\r\\n\\r\\nContext comes from persisted ReviewLens data.\\r\\nContext belongs to the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nContext belongs to the authenticated user.\\r\\nContext does not accidentally include a previously selected target.\\r\\nThe team should document important context-size or model-token limitations.\\r\\n\\r\\nRules: S2-BR-009, S2-BR-012 through S2-BR-014, S2-BR-022 through S2-BR-026\\r\\n\\r\\nS2-011 - Answer Questions from Review Evidence\\r\\nOutcome: For an in-scope question supported by the active review dataset, ReviewLens produces a useful answer based on those reviews.\\r\\n\\r\\nTechnical Guidance:\\r\\n\\r\\nRepresentative questions might include:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhat complaints appear most frequently?\\r\\nWhat do customers like about this product?\\r\\nAre there recurring complaints about customer service?\\r\\nWhat themes appear in low-rated reviews?\\r\\nWhat reasons do reviewers give f…5710 tokens truncated…nd failure\\r\\n- External-provider failures\\r\\n- Database failures\\r\\n- Unexpected application failures\\r\\n\\r\\nLogs should include safe context such as operation name, error category, and a request or correlation identifier when available.\\r\\n\\r\\nNever log:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Passwords\\r\\n- Session cookies, authentication tokens, or authorization headers\\r\\n- API keys, database credentials, or complete environment values\\r\\n- Supabase service-role keys\\r\\n- Unredacted personal information\\r\\n- Full customer-review text in routine production logs\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the shared project logger once it is established. Do not leave temporary `console.log` debugging statements in merged code.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 10. Adding and Updating Dependencies\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team uses npm and commits `package-lock.json`. Do not use Yarn or pnpm in this repository.\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore adding a dependency:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Confirm that it solves a specific project need.\\r\\n2. Confirm that an existing dependency or platform capability does not already solve the problem.\\r\\n3. Verify that the package is actively maintained and compatible with the project's Node.js and Next.js versions.\\r\\n4. Review its license and known security concerns.\\r\\n5. Place it in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` correctly.\\r\\n6. Explain the addition in the pull request.\\r\\n\\r\\nInstall packages through npm rather than manually editing dependency versions. Unrelated dependency upgrades must not be included in a feature pull request.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 11. Testing Standards\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery code change that adds or modifies behavior must include appropriate automated tests. Documentation-only changes should state that automated tests are not applicable and identify the review performed instead.\\r\\n\\r\\nDepending on the behavior, tests should cover:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Successful behavior\\r\\n- Expected failure behavior\\r\\n- Validation boundaries\\r\\n- Authenticated and unauthenticated requests\\r\\n- Authorized and unauthorized users\\r\\n- Persistence and ownership where applicable\\r\\n- Loading and error states for interactive UI\\r\\n\\r\\nExternal review-provider APIs and OpenAI calls must be mocked or replaced with deterministic fixtures in CI. Automated tests must not depend entirely on a live external website or paid provider.\\r\\n\\r\\nSecurity-sensitive features require explicit User A/User B isolation tests. A test must demonstrate denial at the backend or database boundary, not merely that the other user's record is hidden in the UI.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 12. AI-Assisted Development\\r\\n\\r\\nAI-generated code is treated as team-authored code and must meet the same standards and Definition of Done.\\r\\n\\r\\nDevelopers must:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Provide the relevant story, architecture, standards, and existing code as prompt context.\\r\\n- Review and understand generated changes before accepting them.\\r\\n- Verify generated APIs, packages, and configuration against authoritative documentation.\\r\\n- Test generated behavior, including failure and security cases.\\r\\n- Retain the required AI-session transcript according to the convention established by S1-004.\\r\\n- Request additional human review for authentication, authorization, RLS, secret handling, ingestion, and AI-data-boundary changes.\\r\\n\\r\\nAI output is a proposal, not proof that a change is correct.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 13. Pull Request Requirements\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery pull request must:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Link the relevant GitHub issue.\\r\\n- Describe what changed and why.\\r\\n- Stay within the assigned story's scope.\\r\\n- Identify tests or review evidence.\\r\\n- Pass all applicable build, formatting, lint, and automated-test checks.\\r\\n- Contain no real secrets or unrelated generated files.\\r\\n- Receive approval from at least one teammate before merge.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe author must respond to review feedback. A pull request is not Done until it is approved, required checks pass, it is merged into `main`, and the associated board item is updated.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 14. Environment and Secret Requirements\\r\\n\\r\\n- Real secrets must never be committed.\\r\\n- Local secrets belong in `.env.local`, which must be ignored by Git.\\r\\n- `.env.example` documents required variable names using empty or clearly fake placeholder values.\\r\\n- Variables beginning with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are exposed to the browser and must never contain private credentials.\\r\\n- Supabase service-role keys, database credentials, OpenAI keys, and private provider credentials are server-only.\\r\\n- Environment-specific values must not be hard-coded into source files.\\r\\n- Missing required configuration must produce a clear startup or runtime error without exposing the secret value.\\r\\n- If a secret is accidentally committed, stop using it, notify the team, rotate or revoke it immediately, and follow the team's incident procedure. Deleting it from the latest file alone is not sufficient.\\r\\n\\r\\nS1-008 owns the final `.env.example`, ignore rules, environment-validation approach, and setup instructions. When S1-008 changes these conventions, this document must remain consistent with that implementation.\\r\\n# ReviewLens AI-Assisted Development and Review Standards\\r\\n\\r\\n**Project:** ReviewLens AI | **Team:** Fantastic Six | **Story:** S1-004 | **Related rules:** S1-BR-004, S1-BR-008, S1-BR-011\\r\\n\\r\\n## Core principle\\r\\n\\r\\nAI-generated code is treated as team-authored code. The developer who prompts, accepts, and commits it is its author and is fully responsible for it. It goes through the same pull request, review, testing, and Definition of Done as hand-written code.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. AI coding tools the team expects to use\\r\\n\\r\\n| Tool          | Typical use                                                                            |\\r\\n| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\\r\\n| Claude (chat) | Design questions, debugging, explaining errors, drafting docs                          |\\r\\n| ChatGPT       | Same as above; second opinion on generated code                                        |\\r\\n| Claude Code   | Agentic coding in the repo (scaffolding, config, tests, CI). Used in S1-005 and S1-007 |\\r\\n| OpenAI Codex  | Agentic coding in the repo. Used in S1-006                                             |\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Context supplied to AI tools\\r\\n\\r\\nContext we will provide (as relevant to the task):\\r\\n\\r\\n- The user story or issue text, including its acceptance criteria and the business rules it touches (for example S1-BR-004, S1-BR-008, S1-BR-011).\\r\\n- The tech stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Supabase PostgreSQL, Supabase Auth, Vercel.\\r\\n- The domain entities and relationships: User â†’ AnalysisTarget â†’ Reviews and IngestionAttempt.\\r\\n- The API model: Next.js route handlers that validate input and enforce authentication and ownership.\\r\\n- The specific files, types, and schema involved, not the whole repository.\\r\\n- Existing conventions: naming, folder structure, error response shape, validation approach.\\r\\n\\r\\nContext we will NOT provide:\\r\\n\\r\\n- API keys, service-role keys, database connection strings, tokens, or `.env` contents.\\r\\n- Real user data, personal information, or private review data that is not approved for sharing.\\r\\n- Credentials of any kind, even \\\"temporary\\\" ones.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a snippet contains a secret, redact it first. If a secret is accidentally pasted into an AI tool, treat it as leaked: rotate it immediately and tell the team.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Reviewing generated code\\r\\n\\r\\n- Before opening a pull request, the author must read and understand every line of generated code. Reviewers apply the same standard.\\r\\n- Understand it. If the author cannot explain a block, it does not get committed.\\r\\n- Check it against the story. The code must do what the acceptance criteria say, and nothing extra.\\r\\n- Check scope. Remove unrelated refactors, unused code, and leftover debugging output.\\r\\n- Check consistency. It must follow existing patterns, naming, and error handling.\\r\\n- Check security basics. Look for missing auth checks, missing ownership checks, unvalidated input, and secrets in code.\\r\\n- Check for hallucination. Confirm that functions, methods, options, and imports actually exist.\\r\\n- At least one teammate other than the author reviews every pull request. The author does not approve their own PR.\\r\\n- The PR description states whether AI assistance was used and which tool.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Validating generated dependencies and APIs\\r\\n\\r\\nAI tools can invent packages, functions, and endpoints, or suggest outdated or unsafe ones.\\r\\n\\r\\n- Verify every new package exists on the official registry, matches the intended name (watch for look-alike or typosquatted names), and is actively maintained.\\r\\n- Check the package's license, weekly downloads, and last release before adding it.\\r\\n- Add a dependency only when it is needed. Prefer what the stack already provides.\\r\\n- Verify every API call, method, or option against the official documentation (Next.js, Supabase, OpenAI), not just the AI's explanation.\\r\\n- Run `npm audit` after adding or updating dependencies and resolve high and critical findings.\\r\\n- Commit the lockfile with the change, and pin or review version ranges.\\r\\n- Never run install scripts or commands from AI output without reading them first.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Testing required before generated code is accepted\\r\\n\\r\\nGenerated code is accepted only when all of the following pass:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass with no new errors.\\r\\n- `npm run format:check` and `npm run lint` pass.\\r\\n- `npm test` passes, and unit tests cover the new logic, including invalid input and failure cases.\\r\\n- Tests exist for the security rules the change touches:\\r\\n  - **S1-BR-004:** a protected endpoint called without a valid session is rejected.\\r\\n  - **S1-BR-008:** a user cannot read, write, update, or ingest data belonging to another user.\\r\\n  - **S1-BR-011:** no secrets or provider credentials appear in source code or browser-delivered bundles.\\r\\n- The author manually exercises the feature (happy path and at least one failure path).\\r\\n- The GitHub Actions check \\\"Lint, typecheck, test, build\\\" (S1-007) passes on the pull request before merge. If CI is unavailable, run the same commands locally and paste the results into the PR.\\r\\n- Tests are written or reviewed by a human. A test that the AI wrote must be read to confirm it actually asserts something meaningful.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 6. Retaining AI session transcripts\\r\\n\\r\\nThe team keeps the complete available transcript of every AI session that produced or shaped committed code. A summary does not replace the original conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Where:** `ai-transcripts/` at the root of the repository.\\r\\n- **Naming:** `YYYY-MM-DD_<author>_<issue-id>_<tool>.md` (for example `2026-11-02_shahdp2_S1-007_claude.md`).\\r\\n- **What to save:** the original prompts and AI responses, including failed approaches, errors, corrections, and dead ends, plus a short note on what was accepted, changed, or rejected.\\r\\n- **Redact first:** remove secrets, credentials, and personal data before committing a transcript.\\r\\n- **Assume visibility:** transcripts are committed to the repository, so assume they may be seen by the whole team and the instructor.\\r\\n- **Link it:** reference the transcript path in the pull request description.\\r\\n- **Retain** transcripts for the duration of the course project. They are part of the project record and may be reviewed by the instructor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 7. When generated code requires additional security review\\r\\n\\r\\nAny pull request that includes AI-generated code in the areas below needs a second reviewer who specifically checks security, in addition to the normal review:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Authentication and sessions.** Any protected backend route must verify the authenticated identity on the server. Hiding frontend controls is not access protection (S1-BR-004).\\r\\n- **Authorization and ownership.** Any code that reads, writes, updates, or deletes user-owned data must enforce ownership server-side, and cross-user operations must be denied (S1-BR-008). Row Level Security must be enabled on all tables holding user data, and its policies must restrict access to the owning user.\\r\\n- **Ingestion.** Any code that parses uploaded CSV/JSON or writes review data, including validation, size limits, and ownership of the target.\\r\\n- **Database access.** SQL, migrations, Row Level Security policies, and any use of a privileged or service-role key.\\r\\n- **Secrets and configuration.** Environment variables, provider credentials, database credentials, review-service credentials, and anything that could end up in client-side code. `.env` files must be in `.gitignore`. Only values a provider explicitly designs to be public (such as the Supabase anon key, exposed through `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables) may reach the browser. The Supabase service-role key and the OpenAI key stay server-side only (S1-BR-011).\\r\\n- **Third-party calls.** Code that calls the OpenAI API or another external service, especially what data is sent.\\r\\n- **New or upgraded dependencies** with network, file-system, or install-script access.\\r\\n- **Error handling.** Responses must not leak stack traces, secret keys, or internal diagnostics to the browser.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Definition of Done (applies equally to AI-generated code)\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Meets the story's acceptance criteria\\r\\n- [ ] Reviewed and approved by a teammate other than the author\\r\\n- [ ] `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass, and the GitHub Actions check \\\"Lint, typecheck, test, build\\\" passes on the PR\\r\\n- [ ] Security rules S1-BR-004, S1-BR-008, and S1-BR-011 verified where applicable\\r\\n- [ ] Dependencies and APIs verified against official sources\\r\\n- [ ] No secrets in source control or Teams may choose their own layout, visual style, and interaction patterns, but those decisions must produce one coherent product from beginning to end.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. How To Use These UX Specifications\\r\\nUse project materials in this order:\\r\\n\\r\\nActive sprint requirements define required sprint scope and grading expectations.\\r\\nThe Product Requirements Document defines overall product direction.\\r\\nThese UX specifications define user-experience standards and consistency expectations.\\r\\nThe technical specifications define implementation standards and engineering guardrails.\\r\\nIf there is a conflict, follow the active sprint requirements for implementation scope.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe most important idea is simple:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application should feel like one product, not three sprint submissions stitched together.\\r\\n\\r\\nUsers should not feel that they are moving between unrelated screens, disconnected workflows, or inconsistent interaction patterns.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. Product Experience Direction\\r\\nReviewLens is an analysis-centered application.\\r\\n\\r\\nEverything in the interface should help a user move from identifying what they want to analyze to understanding the available review evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe primary product flow is:\\r\\n\\r\\nAnalysisTarget â†’ Ingestion â†’ Dataset Summary â†’ Review Q&A\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen a user enters the application, they should be able to understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhat entities they are analyzing.\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget is active.\\r\\nWhich review platform supplied the active data.\\r\\nWhether usable review data exists.\\r\\nWhat the ingestion result means.\\r\\nWhat dataset the summary represents.\\r\\nWhat dataset ReviewLens is using for Q&A.\\r\\nThe application should reduce ambiguity around the analysis context.\\r\\n\\r\\nReviewLens should feel like a focused review-intelligence product, not a general-purpose chatbot.\\r\\n\\r\\n3. Navigation Expectations\\r\\nEach team may choose its navigation pattern.\\r\\n\\r\\nAcceptable approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nTop navigation.\\r\\nLeft navigation.\\r\\nHybrid navigation.\\r\\nAnother coherent design.\\r\\nWhat is not acceptable is changing navigation paradigms arbitrarily across the application.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the application begins with one approach, major screens and workflows should follow that approach consistently.\\r\\n\\r\\nNavigation should make it easy to:\\r\\n\\r\\nFind existing AnalysisTargets.\\r\\nCreate a new AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nOpen the active AnalysisTarget workspace.\\r\\nMove between major product areas without losing context.\\r\\nAccess account or settings functionality when applicable.\\r\\nNot every final destination must appear in every sprint. Follow the active sprint requirements for required functionality.\\r\\n\\r\\nMoving between major application areas should not cause the user to lose track of the active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\n\\r\\n4. AnalysisTarget Workspace\\r\\nThe AnalysisTarget workspace is the primary operating surface for ReviewLens and should receive the most design attention.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is where the user should be able to understand and work with the active analysis context.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe workspace should make clear:\\r\\n\\r\\nTarget or entity name.\\r\\nReview platform.\\r\\nSource or source reference.\\r\\nIngestion state.\\r\\nCurrent review dataset.\\r\\nIngestion summary.\\r\\nAvailable Q&A functionality.\\r\\nTeams may choose how this workspace is organized.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nTabs.\\r\\nPanels.\\r\\nCards.\\r\\nSections.\\r\\nSplit views.\\r\\nAnother coherent model.\\r\\nThe important requirement is that ingestion, summary, and Q&A feel like parts of one analysis workflow rather than unrelated application screens.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user should not need to infer which AnalysisTarget or review dataset is currently being analyzed.\\r\\n\\r\\n5. AnalysisTarget Management Experience\\r\\nCreating, reopening, switching, and managing AnalysisTargets should be straightforward.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should make it easy to:\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a new AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nIdentify the entity being analyzed.\\r\\nIdentify the supported review platform.\\r\\nIdentify the review source.\\r\\nReopen an existing target.\\r\\nSwitch between owned targets.\\r\\nUnderstand which target is active.\\r\\nDelete an owned target when that functionality is available.\\r\\nTarget creation should use clear validation and meaningful feedback.\\r\\n\\r\\nInvalid input should not create confusing partial state.\\r\\n\\r\\nSwitching AnalysisTargets should produce a visible and understandable change in the active application context.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user should never have to guess whether they are still viewing or analyzing the prior target.\\r\\n\\r\\n6. Review Ingestion Experience\\r\\nReview ingestion should not feel like a black box.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen ingestion begins, the user should understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhat source is being processed.\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget will receive the resulting review data.\\r\\nWhether processing is underway.\\r\\nWhether ingestion succeeds.\\r\\nWhether ingestion fails.\\r\\nWhether ingestion partially succeeds, when supported.\\r\\nWhether records were skipped or rejected.\\r\\nWhether the resulting dataset is ready for analysis.\\r\\nThe application should clearly distinguish important states such as:\\r\\n\\r\\nNo ingestion has occurred.\\r\\nIngestion is processing.\\r\\nIngestion succeeded.\\r\\nIngestion failed.\\r\\nIngestion partially succeeded.\\r\\nThe user should not click an ingestion action and then be left wondering whether data was collected or whether ReviewLens is ready to answer questions.\\r\\n\\r\\n6.1 Ingestion Result Summary\\r\\nThe ingestion summary should communicate enough information to give the user confidence in the active dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, the user should be able to understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget the summary represents.\\r\\nHow many reviews were successfully ingested.\\r\\nBasic rating information.\\r\\nWhether records were rejected or skipped when applicable.\\r\\nWhether the active dataset is usable for Q&A.\\r\\nSummary information should be easy to scan.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe UX should not force the user to inspect raw review rows merely to determine whether ingestion worked.\\r\\n\\r\\n7. Review Intelligence and Q&A Experience\\r\\nReviewLens Q&A should feel like analysis of the active review dataset, not open-ended AI chat.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should maintain visible context around:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nThe review platform.\\r\\nThe active dataset.\\r\\nWhether review data is available.\\r\\nWhether the system is ready to answer review-grounded questions.\\r\\nThe Q&A interaction should be simple and focused.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, it should support:\\r\\n\\r\\nNatural-language question input.\\r\\nClear submit action.\\r\\nProcessing or loading state.\\r\\nResponse presentation.\\r\\nMeaningful failure state.\\r\\nPersistent multi-session chat history is not required unless active sprint requirements say otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n7.1 Distinct Q&A Outcomes\\r\\nThe interface should distinguish among four fundamentally different outcomes:\\r\\n\\r\\nGrounded answer\\r\\nReviewLens can answer from the active reviews.\\r\\n\\r\\nInsufficient evidence\\r\\nThe question is relevant, but the available reviews do not support a reliable answer.\\r\\n\\r\\nOut-of-scope refusal\\r\\nThe question is unrelated to the active review dataset or asks about unsupported entities or platforms.\\r\\n\\r\\nAI/service failure\\r\\nThe Q&A operation could not be completed because of a technical or external-service problem.\\r\\n\\r\\nThese should not be treated as interchangeable generic chatbot responses.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user should be able to understand whether ReviewLens:\\r\\n\\r\\nFound evidence.\\r\\nDid not find enough evidence.\\r\\nRefused the request because it was outside scope.\\r\\nFailed because the service could not complete the request.\\r\\n7.2 Make the Analysis Boundary Visible\\r\\nReviewLens should make its boundaries understandable before users repeatedly discover them through failed questions.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should reinforce that ReviewLens answers questions about:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nThe active persisted review dataset.\\r\\nThe application should not visually imply that it is a general-purpose assistant.\\r\\n\\r\\n8. Context Switching and State Clarity\\r\\nChanging AnalysisTargets changes the meaning of the analysis.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe UX must make that transition obvious.\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter switching from one target to another:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe new target should be clearly identified.\\r\\nThe ingestion summary should correspond to the new target.\\r\\nThe review dataset should correspond to the new target.\\r\\nQ&A should clearly operate in the new target's context.\\r\\nPrior-target state should not appear to remain active accidentally.\\r\\nTeams may choose how to handle prior Q&A content.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nClearing prior Q&A when the target changes.\\r\\nKeeping Q&A separated by AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nLabeling prior Q&A clearly as belonging to a different target.\\r\\nAnother coherent design.\\r\\nThe exact design is flexible.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe guardrail is not:\\r\\n\\r\\nNever show historical Q&A.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe guardrail is:\\r\\n\\r\\nNever allow the user to reasonably believe that an answer belongs to one AnalysisTarget when it was generated from another.\\r\\n\\r\\n9. Error and Failure Experience\\r\\nReviewLens depends on multiple application and external-service boundaries, so failure states are part of the normal user experience.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should distinguish among:\\r\\n\\r\\nInvalid AnalysisTarget input.\\r\\nAuthentication or session failure.\\r\\nAuthorization denial.\\r\\nReview-source or ingestion failure.\\r\\nPartial or incomplete ingestion.\\r\\nNo review data available.\\r\\nLLM-provider failure.\\r\\nUnexpected application failure.\\r\\nErrors should be expressed in user terms rather than implementation terms.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not present normal users with:\\r\\n\\r\\nRaw stack traces.\\r\\nDatabase exceptions.\\r\\nProvider SDK errors.\\r\\nInternal authentication-provider messages.\\r\\nSecret values.\\r\\nUnnecessary technical diagnostics.\\r\\nWhere practical, failure messages should also communicate what the user can do next.\\r\\n\\r\\nExamples include:\\r\\n\\r\\nCorrect invalid input.\\r\\nRetry ingestion later.\\r\\nComplete ingestion before asking questions.\\r\\nAsk a question about the active reviews.\\r\\nTry the AI operation again when the provider is available.\\r\\n10. Visual Language\\r\\nThe visual direction should be modern, student-friendly, and professional.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application should feel current without becoming noisy or overly decorative.\\r\\n\\r\\nTeams may choose their own design style, but they should establish a visual system early and apply it consistently.\\r\\n\\r\\nTypography, spacing, color, and component styling should be deliberate.\\r\\n\\r\\nRepeated UI elements should look and behave as though they belong to the same product family.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis includes:\\r\\n\\r\\nButtons.\\r\\nForms.\\r\\nCards and panels.\\r\\nNavigation.\\r\\nStatus indicators.\\r\\nLoading states.\\r\\nValidation.\\r\\nError states.\\r\\nIngestion states.\\r\\nQ&A responses.\\r\\nReviewLens should look like a modern analysis product rather than a collection of developer tools or an unstyled generic chatbot.\\r\\n\\r\\n11. Responsive Behavior\\r\\nReviewLens is desktop-first.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe primary workflows are expected to be used primarily on desktop and laptop computers, and teams should optimize those experiences first.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt the same time, the application should remain usable and understandable on tablets and mobile devices.\\r\\n\\r\\nResponsive support should be intentional rather than an afterthought.\\r\\n\\r\\nCore workflows should not become unusable merely because the screen is smaller.\\r\\n\\r\\nA Progressive Web App implementation is optional.\\r\\n\\r\\nIt may be included if a team chooses to invest in it, but it is not required.\\r\\n\\r\\n12. Production Experience Expectations\\r\\nBy the final sprint, ReviewLens should feel like a production application rather than a development environment exposed to the internet.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe public application should:\\r\\n\\r\\nLoad into a coherent product experience.\\r\\nPreserve the navigation and interaction patterns established earlier.\\r\\nUse deliberate loading states.\\r\\nHandle missing or unavailable external services gracefully.\\r\\nAvoid exposing developer-only debug information.\\r\\nAvoid exposing raw errors or configuration details.\\r\\nPreserve user context and persisted data across sessions.\\r\\nContinue to make the active AnalysisTarget clear.\\r\\nProduction deployment should not introduce an entirely different user experience from the development application.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application should feel like the same product throughout the semester.\\r\\n\\r\\n13. UX Quality Standard\\r\\nThe primary UX quality goals are:\\r\\n\\r\\nConsistency\\r\\nRepeated actions, controls, states, and interaction patterns should behave the same way throughout the application.\\r\\n\\r\\nClarity\\r\\nUsers should understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget is active.\\r\\nWhat review data is available.\\r\\nWhat action they can take.\\r\\nWhat just happened.\\r\\nWhether ReviewLens answered, lacked evidence, refused the question, or encountered a technical failure.\\r\\nFlow\\r\\nUsers should be able to move naturally through:\\r\\n\\r\\nTarget selection â†’ Ingestion â†’ Dataset understanding â†’ Review Q&A\\r\\n\\r\\nwithout becoming lost or losing context.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a team makes creative layout and interaction choices while preserving consistency, clarity, and flow, that is exactly the kind of result this project should produce.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n\"}"

AnalysisTarget Workspace\\r\\nThe AnalysisTarget workspace is the primary operating surface for ReviewLens and should receive the most design attention.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is where the user should be able to understand and work with the active analysis context.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe workspace should make clear:\\r\\n\\r\\nTarget or entity name.\\r\\nReview platform.\\r\\nSource or source reference.\\r\\nIngestion state.\\r\\nCurrent review dataset.\\r\\nIngestion summary.\\r\\nAvailable Q&A functionality.\\r\\nTeams may choose how this workspace is organized.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nTabs.\\r\\nPanels.\\r\\nCards.\\r\\nSections.\\r\\nSplit views.\\r\\nAnother coherent model.\\r\\nThe important requirement is that ingestion, summary, and Q&A feel like parts of one analysis workflow rather than unrelated application screens.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user should not need to infer which AnalysisTarget or review dataset is currently being analyzed.\\r\\n\\r\\n5. AnalysisTarget Management Experience\\r\\nCreating, reopening, switching, and managing AnalysisTargets should be straightforward.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should make it easy to:\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate a new AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nIdentify the entity being analyzed.\\r\\nIdentify the supported review platform.\\r\\nIdentify the review source.\\r\\nReopen an existing target.\\r\\nSwitch between owned targets.\\r\\nUnderstand which target is active.\\r\\nDelete an owned target when that functionality is available.\\r\\nTarget creation should use clear validation and meaningful feedback.\\r\\n\\r\\nInvalid input should not create confusing partial state.\\r\\n\\r\\nSwitching AnalysisTargets should produce a visible and understandable change in the active application context.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user should never have to guess whether they are still viewing or analyzing the prior target.\\r\\n\\r\\n6. Review Ingestion Experience\\r\\nReview ingestion should not feel like a black box.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen ingestion begins, the user should understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhat source is being processed.\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget will receive the resulting review data.\\r\\nWhether processing is underway.\\r\\nWhether ingestion succeeds.\\r\\nWhether ingestion fails.\\r\\nWhether ingestion partially succeeds, when supported.\\r\\nWhether records were skipped or rejected.\\r\\nWhether the resulting dataset is ready for analysis.\\r\\nThe application should clearly distinguish important states such as:\\r\\n\\r\\nNo ingestion has occurred.\\r\\nIngestion is processing.\\r\\nIngestion succeeded.\\r\\nIngestion failed.\\r\\nIngestion partially succeeded.\\r\\nThe user should not click an ingestion action and then be left wondering whether data was collected or whether ReviewLens is ready to answer questions.\\r\\n\\r\\n6.1 Ingestion Result Summary\\r\\nThe ingestion summary should communicate enough information to give the user confidence in the active dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, the user should be able to understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget the summary represents.\\r\\nHow many reviews were successfully ingested.\\r\\nBasic rating information.\\r\\nWhether records were rejected or skipped when applicable.\\r\\nWhether the active dataset is usable for Q&A.\\r\\nSummary information should be easy to scan.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe UX should not force the user to inspect raw review rows merely to determine whether ingestion worked.\\r\\n\\r\\n7. Review Intelligence and Q&A Experience\\r\\nReviewLens Q&A should feel like analysis of the active review dataset, not open-ended AI chat.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should maintain visible context around:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nThe review platform.\\r\\nThe active dataset.\\r\\nWhether review data is available.\\r\\nWhether the system is ready to answer review-grounded questions.\\r\\nThe Q&A interaction should be simple and focused.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, it should support:\\r\\n\\r\\nNatural-language question input.\\r\\nClear submit action.\\r\\nProcessing or loading state.\\r\\nResponse presentation.\\r\\nMeaningful failure state.\\r\\nPersistent multi-session chat history is not required unless active sprint requirements say otherwise.\\r\\n\\r\\n7.1 Distinct Q&A Outcomes\\r\\nThe interface should distinguish among four fundamentally different outcomes:\\r\\n\\r\\nGrounded answer\\r\\nReviewLens can answer from the active reviews.\\r\\n\\r\\nInsufficient evidence\\r\\nThe question is relevant, but the available reviews do not support a reliable answer.\\r\\n\\r\\nOut-of-scope refusal\\r\\nThe question is unrelated to the active review dataset or asks about unsupported entities or platforms.\\r\\n\\r\\nAI/service failure\\r\\nThe Q&A operation could not be completed because of a technical or external-service problem.\\r\\n\\r\\nThese should not be treated as interchangeable generic chatbot responses.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user should be able to understand whether ReviewLens:\\r\\n\\r\\nFound evidence.\\r\\nDid not find enough evidence.\\r\\nRefused the request because it was outside scope.\\r\\nFailed because the service could not complete the request.\\r\\n7.2 Make the Analysis Boundary Visible\\r\\nReviewLens should make its boundaries understandable before users repeatedly discover them through failed questions.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should reinforce that ReviewLens answers questions about:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe active AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nThe active persisted review dataset.\\r\\nThe application should not visually imply that it is a general-purpose assistant.\\r\\n\\r\\n8. Context Switching and State Clarity\\r\\nChanging AnalysisTargets changes the meaning of the analysis.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe UX must make that transition obvious.\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter switching from one target to another:\\r\\n\\r\\nThe new target should be clearly identified.\\r\\nThe ingestion summary should correspond to the new target.\\r\\nThe review dataset should correspond to the new target.\\r\\nQ&A should clearly operate in the new target's context.\\r\\nPrior-target state should not appear to remain active accidentally.\\r\\nTeams may choose how to handle prior Q&A content.\\r\\n\\r\\nPossible approaches include:\\r\\n\\r\\nClearing prior Q&A when the target changes.\\r\\nKeeping Q&A separated by AnalysisTarget.\\r\\nLabeling prior Q&A clearly as belonging to a different target.\\r\\nAnother coherent design.\\r\\nThe exact design is flexible.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe guardrail is not:\\r\\n\\r\\nNever show historical Q&A.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe guardrail is:\\r\\n\\r\\nNever allow the user to reasonably believe that an answer belongs to one AnalysisTarget when it was generated from another.\\r\\n\\r\\n9. Error and Failure Experience\\r\\nReviewLens depends on multiple application and external-service boundaries, so failure states are part of the normal user experience.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe interface should distinguish among:\\r\\n\\r\\nInvalid AnalysisTarget input.\\r\\nAuthentication or session failure.\\r\\nAuthorization denial.\\r\\nReview-source or ingestion failure.\\r\\nPartial or incomplete ingestion.\\r\\nNo review data available.\\r\\nLLM-provider failure.\\r\\nUnexpected application failure.\\r\\nErrors should be expressed in user terms rather than implementation terms.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not present normal users with:\\r\\n\\r\\nRaw stack traces.\\r\\nDatabase exceptions.\\r\\nProvider SDK errors.\\r\\nInternal authentication-provider messages.\\r\\nSecret values.\\r\\nUnnecessary technical diagnostics.\\r\\nWhere practical, failure messages should also communicate what the user can do next.\\r\\n\\r\\nExamples include:\\r\\n\\r\\nCorrect invalid input.\\r\\nRetry ingestion later.\\r\\nComplete ingestion before asking questions.\\r\\nAsk a question about the active reviews.\\r\\nTry the AI operation again when the provider is available.\\r\\n10. Visual Language\\r\\nThe visual direction should be modern, student-friendly, and professional.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application should feel current without becoming noisy or overly decorative.\\r\\n\\r\\nTeams may choose their own design style, but they should establish a visual system early and apply it consistently.\\r\\n\\r\\nTypography, spacing, color, and component styling should be deliberate.\\r\\n\\r\\nRepeated UI elements should look and behave as though they belong to the same product family.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis includes:\\r\\n\\r\\nButtons.\\r\\nForms.\\r\\nCards and panels.\\r\\nNavigation.\\r\\nStatus indicators.\\r\\nLoading states.\\r\\nValidation.\\r\\nError states.\\r\\nIngestion states.\\r\\nQ&A responses.\\r\\nReviewLens should look like a modern analysis product rather than a collection of developer tools or an unstyled generic chatbot.\\r\\n\\r\\n11. Responsive Behavior\\r\\nReviewLens is desktop-first.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe primary workflows are expected to be used primarily on desktop and laptop computers, and teams should optimize those experiences first.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt the same time, the application should remain usable and understandable on tablets and mobile devices.\\r\\n\\r\\nResponsive support should be intentional rather than an afterthought.\\r\\n\\r\\nCore workflows should not become unusable merely because the screen is smaller.\\r\\n\\r\\nA Progressive Web App implementation is optional.\\r\\n\\r\\nIt may be included if a team chooses to invest in it, but it is not required.\\r\\n\\r\\n12. Production Experience Expectations\\r\\nBy the final sprint, ReviewLens should feel like a production application rather than a development environment exposed to the internet.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe public application should:\\r\\n\\r\\nLoad into a coherent product experience.\\r\\nPreserve the navigation and interaction patterns established earlier.\\r\\nUse deliberate loading states.\\r\\nHandle missing or unavailable external services gracefully.\\r\\nAvoid exposing developer-only debug information.\\r\\nAvoid exposing raw errors or configuration details.\\r\\nPreserve user context and persisted data across sessions.\\r\\nContinue to make the active AnalysisTarget clear.\\r\\nProduction deployment should not introduce an entirely different user experience from the development application.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe application should feel like the same product throughout the semester.\\r\\n\\r\\n13. UX Quality Standard\\r\\nThe primary UX quality goals are:\\r\\n\\r\\nConsistency\\r\\nRepeated actions, controls, states, and interaction patterns should behave the same way throughout the application.\\r\\n\\r\\nClarity\\r\\nUsers should understand:\\r\\n\\r\\nWhich AnalysisTarget is active.\\r\\nWhat review data is available.\\r\\nWhat action they can take.\\r\\nWhat just happened.\\r\\nWhether ReviewLens answered, lacked evidence, refused the question, or encountered a technical failure.\\r\\nFlow\\r\\nUsers should be able to move naturally through:\\r\\n\\r\\nTarget selection â†’ Ingestion â†’ Dataset understanding â†’ Review Q&A\\r\\n\\r\\nwithout becoming lost or losing context.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a team makes creative layout and interaction choices while preserving consistency, clarity, and flow, that is exactly the kind of result this project should Review-Grounded Q&A\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nS2-009 - Build the Review Q&A Interface\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nOutcome: A user can submit a natural-language question from the active AnalysisTarget workspace and receive a ReviewLens response.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nTechnical Guidance:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nAt minimum, the interface should include:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nQuestion input.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nSubmit action.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nProcessing/loading state.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nResponse display.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nMeaningful error state if the AI request fails.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nA full persistent chat-history system is not required.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nA simple question-and-response interaction is acceptable if it supports the required analysis workflow.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThe active AnalysisTarget must remain clear while the user asks questions.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nRules: S2-BR-008, S2-BR-014\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nS2-010 - Build Review Dataset Context for Q&A\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nOutcome: Before a question is submitted to the LLM, ReviewLens constructs AI context from reviews belonging to the active AnalysisTarget.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nTechnical Guidance:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThe team must make an explicit architectural decision for selecting and supplying review context.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nPossible approaches include:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nSupplying all reviews when the dataset is small enough.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nSelecting relevant reviews before model invocation.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nRetrieval-Augmented Generation.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nEmbeddings and vector search.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nSearch or filtering strategies.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nAnother defensible approach appropriate to the team's dataset size.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nNo particular retrieval architecture is required.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThe implementation must ensure:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nContext comes from persisted ReviewLens data.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nContext belongs to the active AnalysisTarget.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nContext belongs to the authenticated user.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nContext does not accidentally include a previously selected target.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThe team should document important context-size or model-token limitations.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nRules: S2-BR-009, S2-BR-012 through S2-BR-014, S2-BR-022 through S2-BR-026\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nS2-011 - Answer Questions from Review Evidence\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nOutcome: For an in-scope question supported by the active review dataset, ReviewLens produces a useful answer based on those reviews.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nTechnical Guidance:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nRepresentative questions might include:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nWhat complaints appear most frequently?\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nWhat do customers like about this product?\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nAre there recurring complaints about customer service?\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nWhat themes appear in low-rated reviews?\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nWhat reasons do reviewers give for high ratings?\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThe exact wording and presentation of answers are team design decisions.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThe team should design the system prompt and review context so that the model treats supplied reviews as its evidence base.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThe application is not expected to produce mathematically perfect natural-language analysis, but answers should be defensibly connected to the review content.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nRules: S2-BR-008 through S2-BR-014\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nS2-012 - Define and Apply the ReviewLens System Prompt,\\\"**Outcome:**\\r\\n---\\r\\ntitle: route.js\\r\\ndescription: API reference for the route.js special file.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nRoute Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts filename=\\\"route.ts\\\" switcher\\r\\nexport async function GET() {\\r\\n  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n```js filename=\\\"route.js\\\" switcher\\r\\nexport async function GET() {\\r\\n  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Reference\\r\\n\\r\\n### HTTP Methods\\r\\n\\r\\nA **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts filename=\\\"route.ts\\\" switcher\\r\\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function HEAD(request: Request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function PUT(request: Request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function DELETE(request: Request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function PATCH(request: Request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\n// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.\\r\\nexport async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n```js filename=\\\"route.js\\\" switcher\\r\\nexport async function GET(request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function HEAD(request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function POST(request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function PUT(request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function DELETE(request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function PATCH(request) {}\\r\\n\\r\\n// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.\\r\\nexport async function OPTIONS(request) {}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Parameters\\r\\n\\r\\n#### `request` (optional)\\r\\n\\r\\nThe `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`.\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts filename=\\\"route.ts\\\" switcher\\r\\nimport type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\\r\\n  const url = request.nextUrl\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n```js filename=\\\"route.js\\\" switcher\\r\\nexport async function GET(request) {\\r\\n  const url = request.nextUrl\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n#### `context` (optional)\\r\\n\\r\\n- **`params`**: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route.\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts filename=\\\"app/dashboard/[team]/route.ts\\\" switcher\\r\\nexport async function GET(\\r\\n  request: Request,\\r\\n  { params }: { params: Promise<{ team: string }> }\\r\\n) {\\r\\n  const { team } = await params\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n```js filename=\\\"app/dashboard/[team]/route.js\\\" switcher\\r\\nexport async function GET(request, { params }) {\\r\\n  const { team } = await params\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n| Example                          | URL            | `params`                           |\\r\\n| -------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |\\r\\n| `app/dashboard/[team]/route.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |\\r\\n| `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |\\r\\n| `app/blog/[...slug]/route.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Route Context Helper\\r\\n\\r\\nYou can type the Route Handler context using `RouteContext` to get strongly typed `params` from a route literal. `RouteContext` is a globally available helper.\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts filename=\\\"app/users/[id]/route.ts\\\"\\r\\nimport type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/users/[id]'>) {\\r\\n  const { id } = await ctx.params\\r\\n  return Response.json({ id })\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n> **Good to know**\\r\\n>\\r\\n> - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.\\r\\n> - After type generation, the `RouteContext` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n### Cookies\\r\\n\\r\\nYou can read or set cookies with [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) from `next/headers`.\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts filename=\\\"route.ts\\\" switcher\\r\\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function GET(request: NextRequest) {\\r\\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\\r\\n\\r\\n  const a = cookieStore.get('a')\\r\\n  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')\\r\\n  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n```js filename=\\\"route.js\\\" switcher\\r\\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function GET(request) {\\r\\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\\r\\n\\r\\n  const a = cookieStore.get('a')\\r\\n  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')\\r\\n  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nAlternatively, you can return a new `Response` using the [`Set-Cookie`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) header.\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts filename=\\\"app/api/route.ts\\\" switcher\\r\\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\\r\\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\\r\\n  const token = cookieStore.get('token')\\r\\n---\\r\\ntitle: use client\\r\\ndescription: Learn how to use the use client directive to render a component on the client.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nThe `'use client'` directive declares an entry point for the components to be rendered on the **client side** and should be used when creating interactive user interfaces (UI) that require client-side JavaScript capabilities, such as state management, event handling, and access to browser APIs. This is a React feature.\\r\\n\\r\\n> **Good to know:**\\r\\n>\\r\\n> You do not need to add the `'use client'` directive to every file that contains Client Components. You only need to add it to the files whose components you want to render directly within Server Components. The `'use client'` directive defines the [server and client boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary), and the components exported from such a file serve as entry points to the client.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\nTo declare an entry point for the Client Components, add the `'use client'` directive **at the top of the file**, before any imports. The directive applies to the entire module and cannot be placed inside a component or function:\\r\\n\\r\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/components/counter.tsx\\\" highlight={1} switcher\\r\\n'use client'\\r\\n\\r\\nimport { useState } from 'react'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport default function Counter() {\\r\\n  const [count, setCount] = useState(0)\\r\\n\\r\\n  return (\\r\\n    <div>\\r\\n      <p>Count: {count}</p>\\r\\n      <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>\\r\\n    </div>\\r\\n  )\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/components/counter.js\\\" highlight={1} switcher\\r\\n'use client'\\r\\n\\r\\nimport { useState } from 'react'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport default function Counter() {\\r\\n  const [count, setCount] = useState(0)\\r\\n\\r\\n  return (\\r\\n    <div>\\r\\n      <p>Count: {count}</p>\\r\\n      <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button>\\r\\n    </div>\\r\\n  )\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen using the `'use client'` directive, the props of the Client Components must be [serializable](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types). This means the props need to be in a format that React can serialize when sending data from the server to the client.\\r\\n\\r\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/components/counter.tsx\\\" highlight={4} switcher\\r\\n'use client'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport default function Counter({\\r\\n  onClick /* âŒ Function is not serializable */,\\r\\n}) {\\r\\n  return (\\r\\n    <div>\\r\\n      <button onClick={onClick}>Increment</button>\\r\\n    </div>\\r\\n  )\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n```jsx filename=\\\"app/components/counter.js\\\" highlight={4} switcher\\r\\n'use client'\\r\\n\\r\\nexport default function Counter({\\r\\n  onClick /* âŒ Function is not serializable */,\\r\\n}) {\\r\\n  return (\\r\\n    <div>\\r\\n      <button onClick={onClick}>Increment</button>\\r\\n    </div>\\r\\n  )\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Nesting Client Components within Server Components\\r\\n\\r\\nCombining Server and Client Components allows you to build applications that are both performant and interactive:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Server Components**: Use for static content, data fetching, and SEO-friendly elements.\\r\\n2. **Client Components**: Use for interactive elements that require state, effects, or browser APIs.\\r\\n3. **Component composition**: Nest Client Components within Server Components as needed for a clear separation of server and client logic.\\r\\n\\r\\nIn the following example:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `Header` is a Server Component handling static content.\\r\\n- `Counter` is a Client Component enabling interactivity within the page.\\r\\n\\r\\n```tsx filename=\\\"app/page.tsx\\\" highlight={2,8} switcher\\r\\nimport Header from './header'\\r\\nimport Counter from './counter' // This is a Client Component\\r\\n\\r\\nexport default function Page() {\\r\\n  return (\\r\\n    <div>\\r\\n      <Header />\\r\\n\"}"

Functional Requirements\\r\\n4.1 Authentication and Ownership\\r\\nUsers can register, login, logout, and reset password.\\r\\nProtected application routes require authenticated access.\\r\\nBackend services enforce data ownership boundaries for all user-scoped entities.\\r\\nCross-user read/write attempts are denied.\\r\\nReview data belonging to one user must never be included in another user's AI context.\\r\\nAcceptance Criteria\\r\\nAn unauthenticated user cannot access protected analysis data or Q&A functionality.\\r\\nUser A cannot read, modify, delete, ingest into, or query User B's analysis targets or reviews.\\r\\nDuplicate registration email is rejected.\\r\\nSession invalidates cleanly on logout.\\r\\nAuthorization is enforced by the backend and is not dependent only on hidden UI controls or client-supplied ownership identifiers.\\r\\n4.2 Analysis Targets and Review Ingestion\\r\\nAnalysis Target Minimums\\r\\nEach analysis target must include enough information to required by the team's ingestion approach.\\r\\nOwner identity.\\r\\nIngestion Requirements\\r\\nThe application accepts a target URL from the team's supported platform and extracts relevant review data, or allows the user to supply that platform's review data in a practical supported format for analysis.\\r\\nAt minimum, successfully ingested reviews include:\\r\\nrating\\r\\nwritten review text\\r\\nThe system preserves enough source metadata to associate ingested reviews with the correct analysis target and ingestion operation.\\r\\nIngested data is persisted on the backend and scoped to the authenticated user.\\r\\nInvalid, unsupported, incomplete, or failed ingestion attempts produce meaningful user-facing errors.\\r\\nThe application must not present fabricated review data as though it was collected from the selected source.\\r\\nAcceptance Criteria\\r\\nA user can create an analysis target for the team's supported platform.\\r\\nA user can successfully ingest or import a valid review dataset.\\r\\nPersisted reviews remain associated with the correct authenticated user and analysis target.\\r\\nInvalid source input or unusable review data is rejected or reported clearly.\\r\\nA user cannot ingest into or modify another user's analysis target.\\r\\nThe source platform and target being analyzed remain identifiable after ingestion.\\r\\n4.3 Ingestion Result Summary\\r\\nAfter ingestion, the application must give the user a clear summary of what was successfully collected.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe summary exists to give the user confidence that the dataset is accurate enough, sufficiently complete, and ready for analysis.\\r\\n\\r\\nAt minimum, the summary should communicate:\\r\\n\\r\\nAnalysis target and source platform.\\r\\nNumber of reviews successfully ingested.\\r\\nBasic rating information appropriate to the source data.\\r\\nAny reviews or records that were skipped, rejected, or could not be processed, when applicable.\\r\\nThe state or result of the ingestion operation.\\r\\nThe exact presentation may be text-based, tabular, visual, or a combination.\\r\\n\\r\\nSummary values must be derived from the ingested data rather than generated speculatively by an LLM.\\r\\n\\r\\nAcceptance Criteria\\r\\nThe user can distinguish a successful ingestion from a partial or failed ingestion.\\r\\nDisplayed counts and rating summaries agree with persisted review data.\\r\\nThe summary identifies the dataset that will be used by Q&A.\\r\\nPartial ingestion does not silently appear to be complete.\\r\\nThe user can proceed from the completed summary into review analysis.\\r\\n4.4 Guardrailed Q&A Interface\\r\\nInteractive Review Q&A\\r\\nThe application provides a user-facing conversational interface.\\r\\nUsers can ask natural-language questions about the currently selected ingested review dataset.\\r\\nAnswers must be grounded in the review data available to that authenticated user and selected analysis target.\\r\\nIf the ingested reviews do not support an answer, the application should say so rather than inventing information.\\r\\nScope Guard Enforcement\\r\\nThe Q&A experience must explicitly reject questions outside the active review dataset.\\r\\n\\r\\nOut-of-scope requests include:\\r\\n\\r\\nQuestions about another review platform when that platform is not the active source.\\r\\nQuestions about another product or entity that is not represented in the selected review dataset.\\r\\nGeneral world-knowledge questions unrelated to the reviews.\\r\\nRequests that would require another user's review data.\\r\\nScope enforcement should be driven primarily by the LLM system prompt and the application context supplied to the model.\\r\\n\\r\\nSupporting application logic may reinforce the scope boundary, but it must not replace a clear prompt-level scope definition.\\r\\n\\r\\nAcceptance Criteria\\r\\nAn in-scope question receives an answer based on the ingested reviews.\\r\\nAn out-of-scope question receives a clear, graceful refusal or scope reminder.\\r\\nA general-knowledge question unrelated to the review dataset is declined.\\r\\nThe assistant does not claim knowledge of reviews that were not part of the active dataset.\\r\\nChanging the selected analysis target changes the review context used by Q&A.\\r\\nCross-user review data is never exposed through the Q&A interface.\\r\\n4.5 Analysis Target Management\\r\\nUsers can view the analysis targets that belong to their account.\\r\\nUsers can open a target to review its ingestion state and enter the Analysis Workspace.\\r\\nUsers can delete or otherwise remove targets that they own.\\r\\nTarget-management operations enforce backend ownership rules.\\r\\nThe application provides a coherent path for updating or re-running ingestion when supported by the team's design.\\r\\nAcceptance Criteria\\r\\nA user's target list contains only targets owned by that user.\\r\\nOpening a target loads the correct persisted review context.\\r\\nDeleting or updating a target does not affect another user's data.\\r\\nThe UI clearly indicates which target is active during ingestion, summary, and Q&A.\\r\\n5. S2-011 requires answers that are defensibly\\r\\n    connected to the reviews, so an uncited \\\"answer\\\" is treated as a general-knowledge guess.\\r\\n- `UNEXPECTED_CITATIONS`: `insufficient_evidence` or any decline outcome that cites reviews, even\\r\\n  valid ones. End-to-end tests belong under `tests/e2e`.\\r\\n- `public`, `package.json`, lockfiles, environment templates, and framework configuration remain at the repository root as required by Next.js.\\r\\n- With Next.js 16, request proxy logic uses `src/proxy.ts`. Naming Conventions\\r\\n\\r\\n- React component names and component files use PascalCase, for example `TargetCard.tsx`.\\r\\n- Functions, variables, and object properties use camelCase.\\r\\n- Custom React hooks begin with `use`, for example `useAnalysisTargets.ts`.\\r\\n- Constants that are truly fixed application-wide values use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.\\r\\n- Non-component TypeScript files and feature folders use lowercase kebab-case, for example `review-parser.ts` and `analysis-targets`.\\r\\n- Test files use `.test.ts` or `.test.tsx`. Playwright files use `.spec.ts`.\\r\\n- Next.js special files keep their required framework names, including `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, and `route.ts`.\\r\\n- PostgreSQL tables and columns use snake_case.\\r\\n- Domain terminology must be consistent: use `AnalysisTarget`, `Review`, and `IngestionAttempt` in TypeScript and the corresponding snake_case names in the database.\\r\\n\\r\\nNames should describe intent. Authentication, Authorization, and Ownership\\r\\n\\r\\n- Every AnalysisTarget belongs to exactly one authenticated user.\\r\\n- Review and IngestionAttempt access is authorized through the owning AnalysisTarget.\\r\\n- Protected Route Handlers must verify the session, derive authenticated identity, verify resource ownership, and only then perform the operation.\\r\\n- The frontend may improve navigation by hiding unavailable actions, but frontend filtering is never an authorization control.\\r\\n- Client-supplied `userId`, `ownerId`, or equivalent values are not trusted for ownership decisions.\\r\\n- Supabase RLS provides defense in depth but does not replace authorization inside protected server operations.\\r\\n- Cross-user tests must use at least two identities and prove that User B cannot read, modify, delete, or ingest into User A's resources.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 9. The Supabase service-role key and the OpenAI key stay server-side only (S1-BR-011).\\r\\n- **Third-party calls.** Code that calls the OpenAI API or another external service, especially what data is sent.\\r\\n- **New or upgraded dependencies** with network, file-system, or install-script access.\\r\\n- **Error handling.** Responses must not leak stack traces, secret keys, or internal diagnostics to the browser.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Definition of Done (applies equally to AI-generated code)\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Meets the story's acceptance criteria\\r\\n- [ ] Reviewed and approved by a teammate other than the author\\r\\n- [ ] `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass, and the GitHub Actions check \\\"Lint, typecheck, test, build\\\" passes on the PR\\r\\n- [ ] Security rules S1-BR-004, S1-BR-008, and S1-BR-011 verified where applicable\\r\\n- [ ] Dependencies and APIs verified against official sources\\r\\n- [ ] No secrets in source control or client-delivered code\\r\\n- [ ] AI session transcript saved and linked in the PR (if AI was used)\\r\\n# S1-011: Ownership from authenticated identity\\r\\n\\r\\n## Decision\\r\\n\\r\\nReviewLens stores the Supabase Auth user ID (`auth.users.id`) as the owner of user-owned records.\\r\\nThis is the \\\"provider user identifier stored as owner\\\" approach from the story. There is no separate\\r\\ninternal User table, because nothing in Sprint 1 needs profile data that Supabase Auth doesn't hold.\\r\\n\\r\\nOwnership is enforced at two independent layers:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Application:** the Route Handler takes the owner only from `requireApiUser()`, which verifies\\r\\n   the session with Supabase Auth on each request.\\r\\n2. **Database:** Row Level Security requires `auth.uid() = owner_id`, using a client that carries the\\r\\n   user's session. A service-role client bypasses this and must not be used for user requests.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules for user-owned records\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never read an owner from the request. `ownerId`, `userId`, and similar body fields are ignored, not\\r\\n  rejected, so a spoofed value has no effect.\\r\\n- Pass only validated fields to persistence. Reviews and ingestion attempts inherit ownership through\\r\\n  their parent target, as the engineering standards (section 8) describe. S1-013 and S1-022 own that\\r\\n  parent check and its tests.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implemented endpoint\\r\\n\\r\\n`POST /api/analysis-targets` accepts `{ name, sourceUrl }` and matches the S1-015 client contract:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Status | When                                      | `error.code`                      |\\r\\n| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |\\r\\n| 201    | Target committed; `data` is the target    | —                                 |\\r\\n| 400    | Invalid or malformed input; nothing saved | `INVALID_ANALYSIS_TARGET_INPUT`   |\\r\\n| 401    | No valid session; nothing saved           | `AUTH_REQUIRED`                   |\\r\\n| 503    | Identity could not be verified            | `AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`                |\\r\\n| 500    | Unexpected or persistence failure         | `ANALYSIS_TARGET_CREATION_FAILED` |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verification\\r\\n\\r\\n- `tests/unit/app/api/analysis-targets/route.test.ts` runs the real guard, validator, and repository\\r\\n  with a fake database client and asserts the exact row sent to Supabase.\\r\\n- `npm run test:db` proves at PostgreSQL that RLS rejects a row whose owner isn't the current user.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Hosted verification\\r\\n\\r\\nThe endpoint was verified against the shared Supabase project at commit `76fccb2`. The S1-015 form was not part of this verification.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a session expires between `requireApiUser()` and the insert, RLS rejects the write and the user\\r\\ngets a 500 rather than a 401.\\r\\n\\r\\n  return `You are ReviewLens, an assistant that analyzes one set of customer reviews.\\r\\n\\r\\nACTIVE DATASET\\r\\n- Entity being ana…665 tokens truncated…orm\\\": the question is about reviews from a different platform.\\r\\n- If more than one decline outcome applies, use the first that matches in this order:\\r\\n  ${declinePriority}. ### 157. assistant

The merge simulation is clean against current `main` (`9533a69`) and S2-011. It found conflicts with the separate S2-010 and S2-013 branches because we copied their files without recording their ancestry. I’ll resolve those locally on `s2-009`, keeping the newer S2-011 prompt implementation; this will create local commits, with no push.

I also found a mismatch with the ownership docs: the Q&A schema rejects extra owner fields, while the docs require ignoring them. I’ll fix that and add JSON content-type enforcement to prevent browser form submissions from triggering model calls.

### 208. assistant

The current audit reports no production dependency vulnerabilities. The development findings come from `glob`, `minimatch`, and `deepmerge`.

Patched releases are available for the first two. `deepmerge` has no upstream patched release for its prototype-poisoning advisory. I’ll use a small, MIT-licensed local patch for Jest’s configuration-merging dependency and test both the exploit cases and Jest compatibility. That patch will still need the project’s independent security review.

### 252. assistant

The new dependency tests caught a second issue: Jest was still resolving a vulnerable nested copy of `deepmerge`. Its prototype-poisoning tests failed, as expected.

Jest now resolves the patched copy, and all six security and compatibility tests pass. The final clean install is running; afterward I’ll rerun the full checks and production-browser tests before drafting the PR text.
